23:38:11 KST

- Category
- World
Lithuania Prepares Strict Six-Hour Time Limit on Russian Transit
Lithuanian lawmaker Arvydas Anušauskas has registered amendments to the Law on the State Border and Its Guard, proposing to cut transit time through Lithuanian territory for Russian citizens down to six hours.
Last year, nearly 13,000 passenger cars with Russian license plates crossed Lithuania under simplified transit documents, according to Delfi on August 17.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
During that time, documented cases of transit abuse jumped sharply, rising from 360 violations in 2024 to 1,493 in 2025. The lawmaker noted that Russian citizens are increasingly violating transit rules while crossing Lithuania.
He emphasized that the proposal does not breach European Union legislation or unilaterally alter the maximum 24-hour limit set by the Council Regulation of 2003.
The draft law explicitly accounts for objective delays, including vehicle breakdowns, traffic accidents, border queues, and bad weather, which allow for longer transit as long as the total travel time does not exceed the EU maximum 24-hour cap.
To enforce compliance, Anušauskas suggests utilizing existing automatic license plate recognition infrastructure to log transit entry, exit, and route deviations in real time.
He also sent a written request to Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius, calling for an immediate evaluation of current transit controls and the creation of a unified government-level strategy regarding simplified transit between mainland Russia and the Kaliningrad region.
In additional appeals to Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys and Interior Minister Martynas Kaltenis, Anušauskas stressed the need for international action.
He stated, "The 2003 EU regulation allowing 24-hour transit was adopted under entirely different geopolitical conditions. Today, Russia is waging Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and carrying out hybrid operations against the European Union. Therefore, I urge the government and responsible ministers to initiate a review of this EU regulation."
His proposed three-tier plan includes strengthening direct transit controls at the national level, coordinating a joint position with Latvia, Estonia, Poland, and other partner states, and submitting a formal request to the European Commission to amend regulatory acts.
If approved by the Seimas, the amendments will take effect on January 1, 2027. The simplified transit mechanism to Kaliningrad operates under agreements between the European Union and Russia, and Lithuanian authorities held interagency functional exercises in February to assess control measures over the route.
On August 5, 2026, Lithuanian border guards detected an unfinished four-meter underground tunnel dug from Belarus beneath a border fence at a depth of 1.5 meters near Latežeris village in the Druskininkai municipality, bringing the total number of subterranean crossing attempts into Lithuania to 12 since the beginning of 2026.

"If it is adopted, the number of sanctioned Russian individuals, companies, and organizations will immediately increase by a third. Pressure must be increased until Russia stops the war," Kallas stated.

The move falls under the framework of the European Union’s Mediterranean naval mission, Operation IRINI. Kallas said the mission has revised its rules of engagement, enabling participating forces to conduct inspections of ships.

Meet Dovbush T40: Ukraine’s Unmanned Aerial System Capable of Reaching Siberia
Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense has codified the domestically produced Dovbush T40 unmanned aerial system (UAS), a strategic-level aircraft with a range of more than 2,000 kilometers.
It can remain airborne for more than 24 hours, giving it sufficient endurance for operations against targets in the Urals and western Siberia, according to the ministry on August 17.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The Dovbush T40 is intended for deep reconnaissance, fire adjustment, and precision strikes against enemy infrastructure, equipment, and personnel at significant distances from the frontline.
During testing, the Dovbush T40 demonstrated the tactical and technical characteristics specified by its developers. The system is equipped with a high-performance engine featuring an electronic fuel injection system and has low radar visibility.
The drone can be used in different strike configurations, including as a strike system or to release munitions. The ministry also highlighted its resistance to electronic warfare and its advanced technological equipment.
The Dovbush T40 was developed and manufactured by a Ukrainian company with extensive experience in producing unmanned aircraft. The company’s Dovbush T20 and Kotyhoroshko systems have been used on the battlefield since 2022 and have demonstrated high effectiveness, according to the ministry.
Drawing on experience with the Dovbush T20, which was designed for medium-range reconnaissance, real-time artillery fire adjustment, and precision strikes, the manufacturer developed the longer-range and more powerful Dovbush T40 strike platform.
The introduction of the Dovbush T40 comes as Ukraine continues to expand its ability to conduct long-range strikes using domestically produced weapons. Recently, Russian media outlet Agentstvo reported that Ukraine has significantly increased its use of domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles against targets in Russia this summer, with the frequency of attacks nearly doubling over the past six months.

No IDF redeployment from Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed, Board of Peace official tells i24NEWS
Israel and Board of Peace agree on Hamas disarmament, destruction of its weapons and tunnels, while two joint working groups will oversee security and humanitarian efforts in Gaza
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and the Board of Peace have agreed that there will be no redeployment of Israeli forces from Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed and the territory is completely demilitarized, a Board of Peace official told i24NEWS.
The understanding was reached during more than three hours of talks Monday between Netanyahu, US President Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner and senior Israeli, American and Board of Peace officials, as the parties moved toward implementing the next stage of Trump’s 20-point Gaza peace plan.
According to the Board of Peace official, Hamas has committed to “fully disarm” and immediately halt all military activity in Gaza, including rearmament and the construction of tunnels.
The agreement stipulates that all weapons, light and heavy, must be collected and permanently decommissioned, while Gaza’s tunnel network must also be dismantled.
https://x.com/i/web/status/2089382403395424552
This post can't be displayed because social networks cookies have been deactivated. You can activate them by clicking .
Israel, meanwhile, will retain what the Board of Peace described as its “full right of self-defense.” If Hamas resumes terrorist activity, violence or attempts to rearm, Israel will retain the right to take action, the official said.
The agreement also means there will be no IDF redeployment from Gaza until Hamas has been fully disarmed and the territory demilitarized. Israeli forces will also not withdraw from the so-called Yellow Line during this stage of the process.
The talks also produced an understanding that reconstruction and broader rehabilitation efforts in Gaza will not move forward until Hamas’ disarmament has been completed.
According to sources familiar with the discussions, Hamas must begin handing over its weapons if it wants to demonstrate that the disarmament process is genuine and viable. The weapons surrendered by Hamas will not be transferred to a future Palestinian governing body. Instead, they will be destroyed.
During the initial phase, Hamas is expected to hand the weapons directly to an American force, with their destruction carried out under the responsibility and supervision of US General Jasper Jeffers.
The Board of Peace said the talks also addressed Israel’s previous commitments under the agreement that helped secure the release of all hostages, including the living hostages and, tragically, the remains of those who were killed.
To coordinate the next phase, Israel and the Board of Peace agreed to establish two joint working groups immediately. One will focus on security and the complete demilitarization of Gaza, while the second will address basic humanitarian needs, including sanitation, clean water and public health.
Sanitation has emerged as an immediate priority amid concerns over deteriorating conditions in Gaza and the risk of disease outbreaks.

The discussions brought together senior Israeli, American and Board of Peace officials. The Board of Peace delegation included senior officials Nikolay Mladenov and Tony Blair, while US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and American military officers also took part.
In an interview with Channel 12, Mladenov warned that dismantling Hamas’ extensive tunnel network could take as long as 10 years, underscoring the scale of the demilitarization challenge facing the parties.
The Board of Peace official said the sides share a broader objective, backed by Trump: creating a “fully demilitarized and deradicalized Gaza” that no longer poses a threat to Israel and where Palestinians can pursue “prosperity and dignity peacefully.”
The agreements mark a move toward the implementation phase of the Gaza roadmap, with Hamas’ complete disarmament emerging as the central condition for any further Israeli redeployment and reconstruction of the Strip.

Virgin Trains moves closer to Eurostar challenge with Channel Tunnel access in UK
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:36:06 UTC
23:36:06 KST

Virgin Trains has taken another step in its bid to position itself as a competitor to high-speed rail operator Eurostar. The company, owned by British businessman Richard Branson, has secured access to the Channel Tunnel in the UK from the end of 2030.
Virgin Trains moves closer to Eurostar challenge with Channel Tunnel access in UK
Virgin received approval in October from the British rail regulator, the ORR, to use the Temple Mills depot. This is the only depot providing access to HS1, the high-speed train line between London and the Channel Tunnel, which connects the UK with mainland Europe.
Now the ORR has also given the green light for track access on HS1. From October 2030 to December 2040, Virgin will be permitted to operate up to 20 return journeys a day between London and the European mainland.
However, Virgin still has a long way to go before it can challenge Eurostar, part-owned by Belgian rail operator NMBS: it must secure track access and safety approvals from the authorities on the other side of the Channel, strike a deal with the Channel Tunnel operator Getlink, and buy suitable trains. It has a preliminary agreement with French train manufacturer Alstom for 12 high-speed trains.
Virgin aims to run services between St Pancras in London and Brussels, Paris and Amsterdam from 2030. It has previously indicated its ambition to expand in France and into Germany and Switzerland.
Eurostar has held a monopoly on operating passenger trains through the Tunnel since it opened in 1994. It is currently only used at around half its maximum capacity. Feight trains and LeShuttle, which carries cars, lorries and buses, also run between Calais and Folkestone.

WONSAN (North Korea), August 17. /TASS/. The Russian frigate Pallada has left North Korea’s port of Wonsan, the ship’s Captain Nikolay Zorchenko told TASS.
"The Pallada’s visit to Wonsan was a complete success. All the goals and tasks set before us have been fully accomplished. Most importantly, we commemorated the 81st anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japanese invaders, visited the memorial to Soviet liberators, attended cultural events in the Kalma tourist zone, visited a food processing plant, established a sister-city relationship with and maintain good relations with Wonsan University, and held sporting events," Zorchenko emphasized.

The atmosphere was truly festive.

The Russian frigate was in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) on a goodwill visit from August 14 to 17, timed to coincide with the 81st anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japanese occupation.
The Pallada is a sailing vessel owned by Dalrybvtuz, an educational institution under the jurisdiction of the Federal Fisheries Agency. Over the course of 36 years of service, the frigate has completed three circumnavigations and nine transoceanic voyages in the waters of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. Over the years, more than 15,000 cadets have undergone training on the vessel. From Wonsan, the sailing ship headed to its home port of Vladivostok, where it will take part in the Eastern Economic Forum events.

Deputy head of Russia's only anti-war party Yabloko sentenced to 11 years over social media posts
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher

Deputy head of Russia's only anti-war party Yabloko sentenced to 11 years over social media posts
A Russian court sentenced Lev Shlosberg, deputy head of the anti-war Yabloko party, to 11 years and one month in prison after finding him guilty of "discrediting the armed forces" and spreading "war fake news".
Source: Russian independent media outlets Mediazona and Meduza
Quote from Mediazona: "Lev Shlosberg was sentenced to 11 years and one month in a penal colony for taking part in debates about the war and reposting an Ekho Moskvy post featuring a Daily Mirror cover… The sentence reflects the combined penalties under the two charges, with Shlosberg's earlier conviction under the law on foreign agents also taken into account."
Details: The fake news case was opened over a repost on Shlosberg's Telegram channel on 25 February 2022 of an Ekho Moskvy post featuring the front page of the British newspaper the Daily Mirror. It showed a bloodied woman and Putin, with the caption: "Her blood… His hands."
The charge of "discrediting the armed forces" relates to a video posted on the Russian social network Odnoklassniki featuring a debate between Shlosberg and historian Yuri Pivovarov, in which Shlosberg argued for "a swift ceasefire in Ukraine".
Mediazona reported that Shlosberg pointed out that the repost on his Telegram channel had been made before Russia introduced the article on "fake news" and that the remarks made during the debate had in fact belonged to his opponent, whose position the politician disputed.
Meduza reported that all three of Shlosberg's lawyers were unable to attend the hearing. However, the judge refused to adjourn it and appointed another lawyer for him, despite the defendant's objections.
The deputy head of Yabloko received his previous sentence in November 2025, when he was given 420 hours of compulsory labour in a case over failure to comply with the obligations of a "foreign agent", a status imposed on Shlosberg in 2023.
Meduza reported that Shlosberg is one of the few Russian politicians who publicly opposed the war while remaining in Russia.
Background:
- Members of Yabloko, Russia's only party with an anti-war position, support a ceasefire, diplomacy and peace, and oppose nuclear war and political repression.
- On 10 August, Yabloko was barred from standing in elections to the State Duma (lower house of Russia's parliament). Russia's Supreme Court issued the ruling after hearing a lawsuit filed by the Rodina party, which accused Yabloko members of extremism and copyright violations.
- It was the first such case in modern Russian history: a party already registered to stand in an election was removed from the ballot.

Lithuania’s border guard chief resigns after cover-up claims over migrant attack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:32:00 UTC
23:32:00 KST

The head of Lithuania’s State Border Guard Service (VSAT), Rustamas Liubajevas, has resigned amid mounting questions over how his agency handled, and reported, a violent incident on the Belarusian border last month, in which migrants allegedly tried to drag one of his officers across the frontier into Belarus.
Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas announced the resignation at a press conference on Monday, saying Liubajevas had made the decision himself.
"No, I certainly didn’t push for it – this was the chief’s own personal decision," the minister told reporters, reading out a statement in which Liubajevas said he did not want to damage the reputation of the service he had led since 2019.
"During his time in charge, the service had to withstand a hybrid migration attack orchestrated by the Belarusian regime, strengthen protection of Lithuania’s and the wider EU’s external border, and operate under exceptional geopolitical tension. His experience, professionalism and ability to hold the service together through difficult periods mattered greatly for our country’s security," Katelynas said.
"But an institution responsible for guarding the state border needs its leadership to have the full confidence of officers, the public and the political leadership. After the border incident, serious questions arose – not only about whether information had been reported promptly, accurately and in full, but about the circumstances of the incident itself."
The minister said he had not asked Liubajevas directly whether he had known about details of the incident that later emerged in the media: "I didn’t ask, but since I was never informed of any additional circumstances throughout, there probably wasn’t much point asking."
He said he had not been expecting the resignation before their meeting, and that a deputy would take over on an interim basis while a permanent replacement is considered. He gave no further comment on the incident itself, noting that both a disciplinary inquiry and a separate pre-trial criminal investigation are under way.
What happened at the border
The incident took place on July 26 near Kapčiamiestis, close to the Belarusian border, when four border guards lay in wait for a group of migrants believed to be digging a tunnel under the frontier.
The tunnel was found and several migrants attempting to cross through it were detained – but reporting since has suggested that roughly 20 more people then emerged and attacked the officers on duty. At the time, only the discovery of the tunnel was made public; the attack itself went unreported.
Further reading
Asked about it last week, Liubajevas had described it as "a routine border incident, the kind that genuinely does happen in our service, and will likely keep happening."
But the news outlet Lrytas subsequently reported that migrants had not simply attacked the officers – a group had tried to drag one of them back across the border into Belarus.
That account was confirmed by Vitalijus Jagminas, head of a trade union representing pre-trial investigation staff, who said the officer had been let go once he managed to break free.
"Certain officers did confirm to us that such an incident took place – that officers were attacked, and that yes, one of them was either carried or dragged towards the other side," Jagminas said.
He accused VSAT’s leadership of only disclosing information it considered favourable. "Anything that might alarm the public, or point to gaps in the system – they don’t talk about that. All of it gets hidden from the public, and this case shows there was an attempt to conceal the truth. We’ve had signals from people that leadership explicitly ordered staff not to discuss or comment on the incident."
The prosecutor’s office initially said it had interviewed everyone involved but held no information about any officer being injured, signed off sick, or dragged across the border. It later reassigned the criminal investigation from VSAT itself – which had originally been investigating the case involving its own officers – to police in the Kaunas region.
Political fallout
Some politicians argued responsibility shouldn’t rest with the chief alone. "There’s a chain of people responsible who need to be properly checked – not just asked questions, but examined to see whether the right actions were actually taken, whether the systems in place are not only on paper but actually working, and whether their effectiveness is assessed every time," said Dainius Gaižauskas, a member of parliament’s national security and defence committee.
The union’s Jagminas went further: "We want change in this system, and for it to become more transparent. We’re not talking about one individual – this is about teamwork, and the whole team needs to go."
Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius had struck a more cautious note before Liubajevas’ resignation, saying it was too early to draw conclusions about individual accountability.
"I think, as things stand, the question of responsibility in Liubajevas’ case is premature. We need to wait for the findings of an objective, impartial internal inquiry, and only once we have that in writing should we decide whether any judgements are needed – including about the leadership," he said.
Laurynas Kasčiūnas, leader of the opposition conservatives, had urged restraint, pointing to Liubajevas’ role in managing the years-long migration crisis engineered by Belarus.
"This is someone who has done a great deal for our country’s security. Even if a mistake was made here, it shouldn’t wipe out everything achieved before it," he said.

Ukrainian troops involved in terrorism against Sahel states – Lavrov
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:31:14 UTC
23:31:14 KST

Ukrainian troops involved in terrorism against Sahel states – Lavrov
Moscow is alarmed by reports that Ukrainian military personnel are involved in operations carried out by illegal armed groups against countries in Africa’s Sahel region, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said.
Speaking after talks with Ghanaian Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on Monday, Lavrov argued that the involvement of serving troops, rather than individual mercenaries, indicated activity conducted at the state level.
The Russian minister also accused former colonial powers of fueling terrorism in Africa. “It is no secret that this is done by France, which directly works with illegal armed groups, arms them, finances them and instructs them,” he said.
“First and foremost, [France] instructs them on creating problems for those countries, in this case in the Sahara-Sahel region, that have decided to finally, completely and irreversibly break with their former colonizers and are consistently pursuing this course,” Lavrov stressed.
Sahel countries have been fighting a jihadist insurgency since 2012, with years of conflict, displacement, and climate-related shocks contributing to a severe humanitarian crisis. In 2023, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger – three military-led former French colonies – established the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) after cutting defense ties with Paris and accusing France of failing to curb the insurgency. The three nations have since strengthened cooperation with Russia. Relations between Bamako and Paris have meanwhile deteriorated further, with Malian officials accusing France of supporting armed groups active in the Sahel.
Ablakwa, meanwhile, described the Sahel as the “global epicenter for terrorism, violent extremism.” He said that Ghana and Russia had agreed to work together to support Niger, Burkina Faso, and Mali in addressing the security challenges facing the region.
The Ghanaian foreign minister also thanked Moscow for supporting a UN resolution that declared transatlantic enslavement a grave crime against humanity. “We see in Russia a reliable partner,” Ablakwa noted.
Russia and Ghana are set to sign an agreement allowing visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic and service passports. Lavrov said the measure is expected to facilitate contacts between the two governments in areas ranging from foreign policy and trade to investment, humanitarian exchanges and education.
Moscow and Accra also agreed to sign a memorandum on cooperation between their media organizations. Ablakwa noted that the initiative would initially establish ties involving RT and Sputnik Africa on the Russian side and Ghana’s GBC, before potentially expanding to private media outlets.

====================================================================================================

INTERVIEW – Amid war, Ukraine's Muslims find strength in interfaith unity: Mufti
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:27:55 UTC
23:27:55 KST

Kanyshai Butun
17 August 2026•Update: 17 August 2026
- Conflict with Russia has brought Ukraine's Muslim and Christian communities closer together, Mufti Murat Suleimanov tells Anadolu
- ‘Our strength lies in our unity, and that is extremely important,’ he says
- Cleric urges international community to pursue justice in both Ukraine and Gaza
Every day, Ukraine's Muslims live with the possibility that the next missile could strike their mosque, home or neighborhood. But as the war has reshaped their lives, it has also reshaped relations between the country's faith communities, forging closer ties between Muslims and Christians, according to Ukraine's leading Muslim cleric.
In an interview with Anadolu, Murat Suleimanov, mufti of the Religious Administration of Muslims of Ukraine, said Muslim and Christian leaders had worked together before 2022 through regular dialogue and joint initiatives, but the war had brought them even closer. 
Ukraine is home to an estimated 500,000 to 2 million Muslims, according to various studies and Islamic organizations. Unlike in many European countries, most are indigenous, with Crimean Tatars making up the largest Muslim community.
Suleimanov said some expected Muslims to remain neutral because the conflict is often viewed as one between two predominantly Christian countries. Instead, he said, Ukraine's Muslim community openly stood with the country.
"As a result, relations between Christians and Muslims have become extremely close," he said.
He also accused Russia of using propaganda to sow divisions by spreading false narratives about tensions between Muslims and Christians.
"Our strength lies in our unity, and that is extremely important,” he said. “We demonstrate this unity when a metropolitan bishop, a priest, a mufti, and an imam stand together and speak with one voice in support of justice."  
Living through war
That unity has developed against the backdrop of daily attacks that have transformed life for Ukraine's Muslim community.
Suleimanov said missile strikes have damaged civilian infrastructure, including mosques in Bakhmut, Sievierodonetsk and Kostiantynivka, forcing some Muslims to relocate so they can continue practicing their faith within established communities.
"As a result, many Muslims have relocated to other areas so they can remain part of a Muslim community, fulfill their religious obligations, attend prayers, hold janazah (funerals), and meet other religious needs," he said.
Despite the disruption, many have chosen to remain in Ukraine because they consider themselves an integral part of the country.
“Those who stayed understand that their role is very important,” he said. "Why? Because we are part of Ukrainian society.”
Suleimanov also stressed the need for a negotiated end to the war.
"Safety is something we deeply value. When you hear missiles every day and live under constant shelling, it becomes your daily reality," he said. “What all of us want is for this war to end and for peace to prevail.” 
Justice beyond Ukraine
For Suleimanov, the principles that unite Ukraine's religious communities should also guide the international response to other conflicts.
"As the mufti of Ukraine and as a Muslim, I also have a responsibility to speak about the genocide in Palestine, in Gaza. That is our duty," he said.
He said justice should not be applied selectively and urged world leaders to continue pursuing dialogue to end wars.
Suleimanov also welcomed support from the Muslim world but said Ukraine's Muslim community deserves greater international attention.
"We hear words of support, but we would like people to speak more about the Muslims of Ukraine," he said.
He also expressed hope for closer cooperation with Türkiye's Directorate of Religious Affairs (Diyanet), saying he was making "every possible effort" to deepen relations.
"We do see that Diyanet provides assistance, including support for Muslims in Ukraine," he said. "I sincerely hope that in the future our cooperation will become broader, stronger and built on even greater mutual trust.”

Ülemiste Centre Director’s challenge brought decathlete Karel Tilga 6,810 euros  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:59 UTC
23:24:59 KST

Nearly 2,600 people took part in the five-kilometre distances of the Ülemiste Night Run on Friday evening, driven not only by the joy of running but also by a charity challenge: to run faster than the director of Ülemiste Centre, Guido Pärnits. The result was a total of 6,810 euros raised in support of decathlete Karel Tilga, the best-placed Estonian at this year’s European Championships.
For every person who crossed the finish line of the five-kilometre distances ahead of Pärnits, Ülemiste Centre added 5 euros in support of Karel Tilga through the Estonian Athletics Association (EKJL). The donation was directed to Tilga because that same week he finished 5th in the decathlon at the European Championships in Birmingham, the best result among Estonians. A total of 1,362 people ran faster than Pärnits, while Pärnits himself completed the distance in 37 minutes and 8 seconds.
“The challenge we set at the Ülemiste Night Run last night was one of those where I was hoping to lose to as many people as possible. Fortunately, the runners did not let me down, and a substantial sum was raised for Estonia’s decathletes,” said director of Ülemiste Centre Guido Pärnits. “Estonian athletes have given our people many powerful emotions and deserve greater support for it. Our challenge is a good example of how the private sector can support Estonian sport and do so in a joyful way.”
Karel Tilga welcomed the support with delight. “It is a wonderful feeling to know that while we were competing in Birmingham, thousands of people in Estonia were running in support of the decathletes. An initiative like this connects elite sport and recreational sport in a very direct way and shows that decathlon genuinely matters to people.” He added: “Grassroots sport and recreational physical activity play an important role in the long-term health of Estonian society. To help secure the future of Estonian decathlon, I will direct 20 per cent of the support I received to Estonian youth combined events.”
In the view of the EKJL, the project connects recreational sport and elite sport in a special way. EKJL President Madis Kallas stressed that supporting elite sport is a joint contribution of the whole society. “Reaching the top in sport and staying there is very costly, which is why the contribution of businesses is extremely important. The initiative of Ülemiste Centre ingeniously ties together grassroots sport and elite sport, giving every runner a chance to become a supporter of Estonian combined events,” said Kallas.
A similar challenge, held for the first time last year, directed its support through the Estonian Olympic Committee’s platform minusportlane.ee to Estonian athletes preparing for the Los Angeles Olympic Games, raising €5,270 in support of top athletes.

Ukraine firm's planned ammunition plant in Lithuania raises hope, security concerns - BNS REPORT  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:53 UTC
23:24:53 KST

BALBIERISKIS - Plans by Ukraine's Dnipro Electromechanical Plant (DEMZ) to build an ammunition assembly facility near Balbieriskis in Lithuania's Prienai district have sparked both economic hopes and security concerns among local residents.
Community representatives say they have lacked direct dialogue with government authorities and the business sector over the Ukrainian defence company's expansion.
Algis Marcinkevicius, chairman of the local community and a member of the Prienai district council, said he learned of DEMZ's plans through the media despite his local role.
"The first reaction was: why do we know nothing when this is practically a done deal?" Marcinkevicius said.
Economy and Innovation Minister Edvinas Griksas and the head of DEMZ signed an investment agreement on Friday. While the exact value of the multi-million-euro investment remains undisclosed, the project is expected to create up to 450 jobs across Alytus and the Prienai district.
DEMZ plans to manufacture metal shell components at the Alytus industrial park, while a 30.6-hectare site in the village of Azuolai in Prienai will host the ammunition assembly plant. Construction is scheduled to begin this autumn, with production slated for late 2025.
HOPES FOR LOCAL EMPLOYMENT
Marcinkevicius said he had spoken with several residents but noted there was no unified stance yet. The 55-member community group has not formally discussed the plans.
"Nobody knows anything for sure. Information only started trickling out in the afternoon. At the moment, I don't sense any political posturing, opposition, or support because opinions are not yet clear," Marcinkevicius said.
"As an individual, I think of the state. I am a long-time civil servant and have had to make many decisions that did not always seem fair to individuals, but state interests must come first," he added.
The community chairman said he would try to convince residents of the plant's benefits but expressed concern that his credibility had been undermined by the lack of prior communication.
"People might listen to me, but my standing is weakened because I feel somewhat deceived. If I tell them I knew nothing and no one spoke to me, they will ask why I am trying to prove anything to them," he said.
Marcinkevicius noted that the site in Azuolai is surrounded by agricultural land, meaning residents would not be directly displaced. However, he raised concerns about heavy transport and the need for infrastructure upgrades, such as paving and strengthening local roads.
He pointed to a large farming operation near the site, suggesting that heavy vehicle traffic would require significant discussion with local agricultural businesses.
"My dream is that 40 jobs would go to local people. That would mean 40 families staying here rather than sending their children to Alytus or Prienai. It would be a boost for both skilled and unskilled workers," Marcinkevicius said.
While acknowledging that the facility could become a target in a conflict, he suggested it might also bring enhanced security compared with a standard factory. "It is clear this is not a mayonnaise factory," he added.
"NO ONE ASKED US"
Local sentiment remains divided. Some fear the facility will increase risks to the town.
Angele Mieliauskiene, a local shopkeeper, said there was no need for the plant. "It would be calmer for people without it. Everyone is happy about the jobs, but the more of this nonsense we have, the greater the threat to the people themselves."
Others view the project as a vital contribution to national security. "It's good for Lithuania's safety. I've served in the military myself, so I see no problem with it," said mechanic Darius Dirvanauskas.
Ona Blazukiene, a 69-year-old cook at the Loreta guesthouse, dismissed fears that the town would become a target, arguing that the entire country would be at risk in the event of aggression.
"Jobs are a plus. It gives people motivation to earn money and a reason to stay. I'm a grandmother and I'm still working; it keeps life interesting," Blazukiene said.
SEEKING THE BAISOGALA MODEL
Some residents hope initial skepticism will fade, citing the Rheinmetall plant in Baisogala as an example of how such projects can boost local economic activity.
The site earmarked for DEMZ was previously considered for a riflemen's union drone training base. Marcinkevicius cited that project as a model for communication, noting that the municipality held meetings and provided detailed plans to the community at the time.
"We had all the information then, and everything went well. I don't know why that project was abandoned, but it is an example of how things should have been handled now," he said.
DEMZ is a major supplier of defence equipment to the Ukrainian military. Since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the company has shifted from civilian to military production and employs around 4,000 people across its divisions.
The Lithuanian project, spanning Alytus and Prienai, is expected to commence this autumn.

Investor demand for the inaugural EUR 2 million bond issue was exceptionally strong: most of the issue was subscribed within the first seven minutes on the BeMyBond platform.
About Capitalica Asset Management:
Capitalica Asset Management is an investment management company established in Lithuania in 2016, with assets under management exceeding EUR 270 million. The company operates in the Baltic real estate market, developing and managing commercial projects with the aim of providing investors with stable, long-term returns through sustainable and value-creating solutions. The company also has substantial experience in the capital markets, having issued and successfully redeemed bonds worth more than EUR 52 million to date.
In Riga, Capitalica Asset Management has already completed the first development phase of the Verde business quarter, comprising two Class A office buildings. They have become a benchmark for contemporary architectural quality in the city, attracting international tenants and receiving several sustainability awards. Two additional Verde buildings are currently under development. Once completed, the total area of the complex will reach 77,000 m². Investment in the Verde project will soon approach EUR 200 million.
About RUUME arhitekti:
RUUME arhitekti is a Riga-based architecture and urbanism practice dedicated to shaping responsible, future-proof urban developments. Its team of 15 professionals specialises in urban planning, residential architecture and mixed-use developments, designing sustainable and inclusive spaces that prioritise the well-being of both current and future generations.
The practice’s approach combines simplicity with excellence, creating environments that enhance urban life and add lasting value to the city. Before the launch of the US-Israeli war against Iran, the Hormuz strait was considered an open, international waterway. It carries significant portions of global energy shipments, as well as other commodities.

Saeima to convene for ceremonial session to mark 35 years since de facto restoration of independence  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:45 UTC
23:24:45 KST

RIGA - On Friday, August 21 - the day that marks 35 years since the restoration of Latvia's independence - Saeima will convene for a ceremonial session, as Saeima Press Service informed LETA.
The meeting will begin at 12 noon.
During the meeting, speeches will be delivered by Saeima Speaker Daiga Mierina (Greens/Farmers) and Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List). Members of the Supreme Council who voted for the restoration of Latvia's independence, the president, and representatives of the foreign diplomatic corps have been invited to attend the meeting.
The ceremonial session will be aired live on Saeima website saeima.lv, the parliament's Facebook and YouTube accounts, as well as on Latvian Television.
Prior to the ceremonial session, members of parliament will participate in a flower-laying ceremony at the Freedom Monument.
On Friday, the original of the constitutional law "On the Statehood of the Republic of Latvia" will be on display at the Saeima building, along with photo exhibition "The Vote That Changed History".
On August 21, 1991, the Supreme Council of the Republic of Latvia passed the constitutional law "On the Statehood of the Republic of Latvia", marking the end of transition to "de facto" independence of Latvia since the declaration "On the Restoration of Independence of the Republic of Latvia" that was adopted on May 4, 1990.
The Supreme Council of the Republic of Latvia passed the law, "acknowledging our responsibility before the nation, the Declaration of May 4, 1990, the results of the popular vote, and the collapse of the constitutional state authority of the USSR on August 19, 1991."
Thus, on August 21, 1991, the Supreme Council of the Republic of Latvia ruled that Latvia is an independent democratic republic, and the sovereign power of the State of Latvia is vested in the people of Latvia.
The bill was signed by the Supreme Council's Chairman Anatolijs Gorbunovs and Secretary Imants Daudiss.

Regulatory Frameworks and Platform Safety in International Gaming
International gaming websites operate under legal licenses granted by recognized global regulatory authorities. Popular gaming hubs like Curaçao, Malta, and Gibraltar supervise these digital operators to ensure fair gaming practices. These regulatory agencies enforce strict data security standards and require regular software audits. Global Licensing Authorities and Legal Protocols
International regulators monitor gaming operators to ensure long-term site security and consumer protection. Jurisdictions like the Malta Gaming Authority evaluate financial solvency and background records before issuing operational certificates. Licensing boards mandate that platforms store user funds in separate bank accounts away from daily operational money. Encryption Standards and Data Protection Systems
Data security remains a vital pillar of international web gaming operations. Reputable global portals deploy end-to-end 256-bit Secure Sockets Layer encryption across all active server connections. Encryption technology converts user data into unreadable code during network transit. Consequently, personal information and payment records remain secure from third-party interception at all times.
Software Architecture and Game Diversity Features
International gaming platforms host massive software libraries designed for high-speed performance on modern web browsers. Table Games and Live Media Streams
Digital table games bring classic card room action to computer screens worldwide. Users can access digital blackjack, roulette, baccarat, and video poker machines with customizable wagering limits. Advanced global platforms also provide live dealer video streams hosted by professional presenters. High-definition video transmission delivers an authentic card room experience without visual lag.
Payment Methods and Transaction Efficiency Standards
International web platforms support a broad variety of payment channels to accommodate global site visitors. Platforms integrate traditional card networks alongside rapid digital wallet services and decentralized blockchain networks. Fast settlement times and flexible transaction limits enhance user convenience across all international markets.
Blockchain Networks and Digital Coin Payouts
Digital coin payments provide high transaction speeds and enhanced personal privacy for web users. Blockchain transactions operate on decentralized public ledgers without central banking intermediaries. Web portals process digital coin payouts quickly, reducing traditional withdrawal waiting periods from days to minutes.
Traditional Financial Payment Systems
Standard payment cards and international wire transfers remain popular choices among traditional web users. These financial tools offer familiar payment steps and comprehensive consumer fraud protection rules. Although bank wire transfers take longer to process, they provide maximum reliability for large financial transfers.
Mobile System Architecture and Technical Care Services
Mobile devices generate over 75% of total internet traffic on global entertainment portals today. Mobile-first engineering ensures that web applications load rapidly on smartphones and tablets using iOS or Android systems. Users do not need to download heavy mobile applications that take up internal phone storage space.
Mobile Browser Execution and Cloud Hosting
Cloud hosting allows games to run smoothly inside mobile web browsers like Safari or Chrome. Responsive page layouts adjust graphic elements, text boxes, and control buttons automatically to fit small phone screens. Touchscreen controls make reel spins and card selections quick, intuitive, and effortless.

Border guards use ground-penetrating radar to search for tunnels beneath Latvian-Belarusian border  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:43 UTC
23:24:43 KST

RIGA - The State Border Guard, in cooperation with the State Police, has begun scanning soil layers along the Latvian-Belarusian border using ground-penetrating radar to search for possible underground tunnels, Marija Luize Ratniece, advisor on communications and administrative matters to Interior Minister Janis Dombrava (National Alliance), told LETA.
The aim of the inspections is to identify possible changes in soil structure and detect locations where underground tunnels or other structures for illegal border crossings may have been built.
The decision to intensify inspections of the border area was made after the first tunnel known to be used by migrants for illegally crossing the Latvian-Belarusian border was discovered in the municipality of Augsdaugava.
Dombrava emphasizes that, following the discovery of the tunnel, a mandate was immediately issued to find technical solutions for inspecting the entire potentially vulnerable border zone.
"Within a few days, through cooperation between the Ministry of the Interior, the State Border Guard, and the State Police, a solution was found, and ground scanning is already underway. The principle is simple: rather than waiting for the next violation, we are actively seeking out and preventing methods used to attempt illegal entry into Latvia," Dombrava said.
Since August 14, border guards, in collaboration with police officers, have been using ground-penetrating radar to examine the soil structure along the Latvian-Belarusian border. The data obtained allow them to identify unusual changes in soil layers and, if necessary, conduct an in-depth inspection of specific locations.
As reported, a tunnel dug by irregular migrants was discovered for the first time last week in the Silene Border Guard Unit’s sector along the Latvian-Belarusian border, Dombrava told reporters.
The minister noted that a group of migrants was discovered through close cooperation between the State Border Guard, the National Armed Forces (NBS), and the State Police. "While trying to trace more precisely how they entered our country, this hidden tunnel was discovered, which is, for now, the first tunnel of its kind in Latvia," said Dombrava.
As LETA was told at the press office of the State Border Guard, on Monday, August 10, in Skrudaliena Parish, Augsdaugava Municipality, border guards discovered 15 individuals who had illegally entered Latvia from Belarus through an underground tunnel that had been dug beneath the border.
As the State Border Guard points out, this is the first instance in which a tunnel has been used to illegally cross the state border into Latvia. No signs of violations had previously been detected at this specific location, and no individuals who had illegally crossed the state border had been detained there.
The 15 individuals were prevented from illegally crossing the state border in accordance with the State Border Guard Law and returned to their country of departure.
As reported, Operation Vilkatis (Werewolf) has been launched in Latvia, during which all relevant agencies will carry out coordinated actions to curb illegal migration, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List) told reporters.

From 1–4 October 2026, the 17th international contemporary art fair ArtVilnius will bring together 70 art galleries from Austria, Denmark, Estonia, France, Germany, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Sweden, Ukraine, and the United Kingdom.
The 17th edition of ArtVilnius will focus on the contemporary art scenes of Vilnius, Warsaw and Vienna, fostering cross-regional exchange and supporting the international visibility of artistic practices.
The fair will once again take place at the Lithuanian Exhibition and Congress Centre Litexpo, the country's leading exhibition venue, just 15 minutes from Vilnius city centre. Each year, ArtVilnius attracts between 18,000 and 23,000 visitors of all ages.
Gallery Selection
The gallery programme in Vienna is represented by Christine König Galerie, one of Austria’s most prominent contemporary art galleries, which has presented conceptual and contemporary art at international fairs for over four decades, and by Galerie Sturm & Schober.
From Warsaw, LETO Gallery – a participant in the first edition of ArtVilnius – returns after nearly a decade, as does Le Guern Gallery. HOS Gallery and Fijewski Gallery, which represent contemporary Polish artists, both make their debut.
First-time participants also include Galerie 3AP (Düsseldorf), Galleri Lundberg-Sandhagen (Stockholm), Tur (Riga), and Galerija Vartai (Vilnius). Returning galleries include KOGO Gallery (Estonia), ISSP (Riga), Galerie Nivet-Carzon (Paris), Galleri NB (Viborg), The Room gallery (Vilnius), OKAPI (Tallinn). The Vilnius Academy of Arts will present six of its galleries, and galleries from Utena, Molėtai, Trakai, Ukmergė, Šiauliai, and Panevėžys will represent the Lithuanian regions.
The founder of ArtVilnius – the Lithuanian Art Gallerists’ Association – celebrates its 30th anniversary this year. It founded ArtVilnius seventeen years ago, and ArtVilnius has since grown into the largest international contemporary art fair in the Baltic States. Many of the association’s member galleries are taking part in the fair this year, among them are DRIFTS, The Rooster Gallery, Terra Recognita, Meno Niša (all Vilnius), Baroti Gallery from Klaipėda and others.
Project Zone
The ArtVilnius’26 Project Zone is curated by Neringa Bumblienė, director of Nida Art Colony of Vilnius Academy of Arts and artistic director and curator of the Vilnius Performance Art Biennial. Institutional participants include Zachęta National Gallery of Art (Warsaw), Poland’s national institution for contemporary art and a long time commissioner of the Polish Pavilion at the Venice Biennale; Galeria Studio (Warsaw), home to a collection of more than 1,000 works of Polish modern and avant-garde art; Gelatin, the renowned Viennese collective known for its humourous performative installations, courtesy of Galerie Meyer Kainer (Vienna); the Rothko Museum (Daugavpils), holding the only original Rothko works in the Baltic States; and the Stasys Museum (Panevėžys), dedicated to the work of Stasys Eidrigevičius. Featured Lithuanian artists include Deimantas Narkevičius, one of Lithuania’s most celebrated artists, who represented Lithuania at the 49th Venice Biennale and won the prestigious Vincent van Gogh award in 2008, and Emilija Škarnulytė, one of the leading artists of her generation, whose work has been widely presented internationally including a recent solo show at Tate St Ives; participation in a group exhibition at Palais de Tokyo in Paris; and winner of the Future Generation Art Prize and the Ars Fennica Award.
Exhibition The Path | Takas 
The Path, the fair’s annual exhibition of sculpture, installation, and performance, is curated for the first time by Vienna-based curator and writer Aliaksei Barysionak. It features eleven artists: from Lithuania, Žygimantas Julijus Bėrontas, Rokas Janušonis, Povilas Jatkevičius, Ūla Šukytė, Kasparas Brazovskis and Vytautas Viržbickas; from Estonia, Anna Mari Liivrand and Bob Bicknell-Knight (Estonia/UK); from Latvia, Anna Egle; from Ukraine, Mariia Kulykivska; and Katsiaryna Miats (Belarus/Lithuania).
Additional programme
The ArtVilnius'26 programme is complemented by ArtVilnius Talks, a series of discussions and panels, with collector Frédéric de Goldschmidt, art advisor Alia Al-Senussi, curator Paco Barragán, and Jemal Inaishvili of the Kvarelli Foundation among the confirmed speakers. 
The fair also offers guided tours with art historians, an educational programme for visitors of all ages, and networking events. The Young Collectors' stand returns, alongside ArtVilnius+, a space dedicated to cultural initiatives. An international jury of art professionals, together with fair visitors, will present awards recognising outstanding galleries, artists, and works presented at the fair. A dedicated VIP programme offers special guests and collectors exclusive events and private visits.

Latvian team wins bird race  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:24 UTC
23:24:24 KST

TALLINN – The 31st Estonian Open bird race, held in Saaremaa, was won by the Latvian team Himantopus Himantopus, who spotted 143 bird species over 14 hours.
Läänemaa, who were defending last year's title, fell short of the winner by just three species.
The Himantopus Himantopus team consisted of Andris Klepers, Mārcis Tīrums, Pēteris Daknis, and Ilze Bojāre. The team has participated in the Estonian Open for 16 years, but this was the first time they secured first place and the travelling trophy.
"On behalf of team HimHim, a big thank you to the organizers and Estbirding for maintaining and developing this wonderful tradition! We will take care of the rather heavy travelling trophy with great respect until the next rally. We have participated in this international birdwatching competition for 16 years, and we finally managed to win. We saw many birds, enjoyed the enchanting landscapes of Saaremaa, and were delighted with how well our route plan worked. It was an honor to compete with such dedicated and knowledgeable birdwatchers," said Andris Klepers, a member of the winning team.
In a tight competition, last year's winner, Läänemaa, took second place with 140 species, with a team consisting of Leho Luigujõe, Sten Lassmann, and Tarvo Valker. The Finnish team Avescapes Oy came in third with 136 species, with members Heikki Eriksson, Jari Laitasalo, Tuomas Seimola, and Roni Väisänen.
"This was a very exciting rally. We expected tough competition and are extremely happy about the Latvians' first win. The day was rich in birds, and the bird diversity on the coast of West Saaremaa was a particularly pleasant surprise," said Tarvo Valker, a member of the Läänemaa team.
During the rally, the teams registered a total of 185 bird species. Among the rarer species spotted were the Crested Lark, the Two-barred Crossbill, and the Yellow-legged Gull.
Saaremaa's own team, 'Tasa ja targu' (Slowly and Surely), participated in the rally for the first time and recorded 97 species. The team included Karl Jakob Toplaan, Ainar Unus, Maris Sepp, and Liis Sepp.
"For our first time, our plan was to take it easy, enjoy it, and gain experience. At first, we proceeded slowly and surely, but as we spotted more species and got closer to our goal of 100, the adrenaline grew and the pace quickened. The last few hours were therefore very intense and exciting. We just missed the 100-species mark this time, but we gained valuable experience and motivation to participate again next year," said Karl Jakob Toplaan.
For the first time in the history of the Estonian Open, a separate eco-category was also held. It was won by team HFK, consisting of Peter Lind, Alari Pajula, and Janne Põlluaas. The team, which travelled by bicycle on Abruka island, covered 24 kilometers and registered 78 bird species.
"When the vehicle mileage limit was removed, we had the idea to do the rally in a green way instead. Half-jokingly, you could say that we made our own small contribution to reducing the rally's environmental footprint. Doing the eco-rally on Abruka was an extremely positive experience, certainly helped by the island's wonderful nature and nice weather. We recommend eco-birdwatching to others and hope that there will be more participants in this category in future rallies," said Peter Lind, a member of the HFK team.
The Estonian Open is the longest-running bird race in Estonia. The competition began at 3 a.m. and ended at 5 p.m. During this time, teams tried to spot as many bird species as possible in Saaremaa, following the principles of fair play and bird welfare.

Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on Uttar Pradesh and 'Mission 2029'

Both Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani secured key positions in the BJP, while Amit Malviya was dropped from the new team.
NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday hit the reset button as party president Nitin Nabin announced a new national team of office-bearers to prepare the party for the upcoming round of assembly elections, leading up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge. The party leaders described the newly constituted team as a strategic blend of seasoned administrative and organisational experience, youthfulness, geographic diversity and comprehensive social inclusion.The list has some high-profile omissions and some surprise comebacks. While Amit Malviya did not find a place in the new team after serving as BJP’s I-T cell head for 11 years, Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani made a grand comeback after staying on the fringes for long.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the newly appointed national office-bearers. "Congratulations to the newly appointed national office bearers of the BJP and those who have been given various responsibilities in the party. This newly appointed team brings together organisational experience, energy and grassroots connect," PM Modi said on X.BJP chief Nitin Nabin called his team a blend of experience and energy that will provide new momentum to the organisation and take forward PM Modi’s vision of 'Viksit Bharat'.
In a post on X, Nabin said, "Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all the newly appointed office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party's National Team. With a blend of experience and energy, this team will give new momentum to the organisation under the guidance of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi.""I am confident that every member, with the spirit of a dedicated karyakarta, will further strengthen the organisation to take forward the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' and the commitment to nation-building to new heights," he further said.
Here are some highlights of Nitin’s “Nabin” team
The overhauled national team has nearly 50 new office-bearers out of the 65 names announced, signalling a significant break from the past.
The new team has widespread representation, accommodating voices from 23 states and Union territories across the country.
Every major faith is respected and accommodated. The national team has one Sikh member, two Christian members and one member each from Muslim, Jain and Parsi communities.
The youngest BJP chief has opted for a relatively young team. Six office-bearers are below 40 years, 15 are in the 40-49 years age group, and 21 are in the 50-59 years age group.
There are three former chief ministers, 12 women and several experienced MPs in important roles
The committee has four tribal representatives from West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and the North-East, two of whom are women.
Special focus has been placed on the northeast region, with three regional leaders from Tripura, Assam and Nagaland and the continuation of a dedicated North-East Coordination Cell.
"Such balanced appointments empower the incoming national president's executive team to operate with a profound awareness of the nation's vast geographical landscape and regional nuances," the BJP said in a statement.
Focus Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, which goes to polls early next year, has been the biggest focus in this BJP reset. As many as 8 leaders from Uttar Pradesh have found a place in Nitin Nabin's team, the most notable being Smriti Irani.Among national vice-presidents, Rekha Verma and Prof Tariq Mansoor are from UP. Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi have been appointed national general secretaries.Two national secretaries and two Morcha presidents are also from UP.
Political comeback of many sidelined faces
BJP’s new national team marks the comeback of several leaders who were on the sidelines in recent times. From former Union minister Smriti Irani and RSS veteran Ram Madhav to former chief ministers Biplab Kumar Deb and Tirath Singh Rawat, several BJP leaders who had either slipped out of the party's top organisational structure or seen their political stock diminish have returned to prominent roles in the new national team.Smriti Irani, whose biggest claim to fame is her victory over Rahul Gandhi in 2019 Lok Sabha elections in Amethi, ending the Gandhi family's decades-long dominance over the constituency, thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."She described her political journey from an "ordinary BJP karyakarta" to one of the party's top organisational posts as "deeply humbling." She thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."The return of Ram Madhav, who has been made a national vice-president, is also significant.A former RSS spokesperson who was deputed to the BJP in 2014, Madhav emerged as one of the party's most influential general secretaries during its first term in power under PM Modi. He played a key role in the BJP's expansion in the northeast and was one of the principal architects of its alliance with the PDP in Jammu and Kashmir after the 2014 assembly polls.His influence waned after the BJP-PDP government collapsed in 2018, and he was dropped as a national general secretary when then BJP president J P Nadda constituted his team in September 2020. He subsequently largely disappeared from the BJP's organisational front line.
The BJP later brought him back to oversee its Jammu and Kashmir assembly election campaign along with Union minister G Kishan Reddy in 2024.
The 2027 test
The first meeting of the Nitin Nabin's new team is scheduled to be held on August 22, news agency ANI reported citing government sources. However, its first test will be in early 2027 when several states, including Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, go to the polls. The BJP has a duanting task at hand in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party and the Congress together pushed it on the backfoot in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Meanwhile, with changes in the party structure announced, all eyes would now be on the possible changed in the Union Cabinet.

Baiba Priedīte appointed Member of the Management Board of Augstsprieguma tīkls responsible for development  - The Baltic Times

The Supervisory Board of Augstsprieguma tīkls AS (AST), Latvia’s transmission system operator, has appointed Baiba Priedīte as a Member of the Management Board responsible for development. She will take up her position at AST on 1 September 2026.
“AST’s strategic priorities are the security and resilience of electricity supply, the development of the transmission grid, and market integration. To achieve these objectives, it is essential for AST to integrate new electricity producers into the transmission grid, connect energy-intensive consumers, develop new interconnections, and continue the digitalisation of the transmission system. The addition of Baiba Priedīte to AST’s management team will make a significant contribution to achieving these objectives,” says Olga Bogdanova, Chair of the AST Supervisory Board.
Baiba Priedīte has almost 20 years of experience in the energy and banking sectors, including experience in managing change and supporting business growth. She served for 10 years as a Member of the Management Board of the energy company Sadales tīkls AS, where she was responsible for strategically important areas including the electricity market, project and process management, technological development, innovation management, electricity metering, and customer service. She has also served as Head of Business Processes at SEB banka AS. B. Priedīte holds a professional master’s degree in business administration (MBA) from Rīga Stradiņš University, as well as a professional qualification in law, specialising in international law, from the RIMPAK Livonija Business Institute.
“At the same time, the Supervisory Board expresses its appreciation to Arnis Daugulis, the outgoing Member of the Management Board responsible for development, for his significant contribution to the successful and secure synchronisation of the Baltic power grids with the Continental European power system. Under his leadership, a number of strategically important infrastructure projects have been implemented, including Latvia’s interconnections with Estonia, synchronous condensers, battery energy storage systems, and Latvia’s main power system control and data centre. He has also overseen the development of network management systems that support the secure operation of the power system,” emphasises O. Bogdanova.
As previously reported, in view of the expiry of Arnis Daugulis’s term of office, the AST Supervisory Board launched an open selection process for the position of Member of the Management Board responsible for development. Mr Daugulis’s term of office ended on 14 July 2026. To ensure continuity in the work of the Management Board, the AST Supervisory Board appointed him as an interim Member of the Management Board from 15 July 2026 until the appointment, following the selection process, of a Member of the Management Board responsible for development for a full term of office. Mr Daugulis will continue to perform the duties of interim Member of the Management Board until 31 August 2026.
From 1 September 2026, AST’s management team will continue to operate with four Management Board members: Rolands Irklis, Chairman of the Management Board, and Management Board members Imants Zviedris, Gatis Junghāns, and Baiba Priedīte.
On the Selection Process for the Management Board Member Responsible for Development
A total of 41 applications were received in the competition announced by the AST Supervisory Board for the position of Management Board Member for Development. In the second round of the competition, the 11 shortlisted candidates were required to prepare their strategic vision on AST’s key future challenges, outlining the main priorities and proposals for their implementation.
The mandatory minimum requirements for candidates included an academic higher education degree or second-level professional higher education in engineering, natural sciences, law, management, information technology or another comparable field. Candidates were also required to have at least three years of continuous work experience in a management position at a medium-sized or large company or institution, as well as experience in managing IT functions or large infrastructure projects with a total value of at least one million euros. Additional preferred requirements included experience in change management and the implementation of innovation, the use of digital and information technologies, process optimisation, improvement and efficiency enhancement, as well as an understanding of current IT development trends, energy sector development trends, the regulatory environment governing the sector and the energy sector as a whole.
In the third round of the selection process, the management competencies of four candidates were assessed in the following areas: results orientation, development orientation, change management, team leadership, and building and maintaining positive relationships. Results orientation and development orientation were identified as the key competencies. The Nomination Committee decided to recommend two candidates who had achieved the highest scores across all three rounds of the selection process for further consideration by the AST Supervisory Board.
The selection and evaluation process for the position of AST Management Board Member for Development was carried out by the Nomination Committee in cooperation with the recruitment company SIA “Eiro Personāls”. Candidates could apply for the competition from 9 March to 30 March 2026.
The selection and evaluation of candidates for the position of AST Management Board Member for Development was carried out by a Nomination Committee composed of Olga Bogdanova, Chair of the AST Supervisory Board; Juris Zīvarts, Member of the AST Supervisory Board; Laura Līne, Legal Counsel at the State Chancellery’s Cross-Sectoral Coordination Department, State-Owned Enterprise Governance Division; Agnese Strode, Head of the Policy Planning Division at the Employers’ Confederation of Latvia; Sigita Škapare, Member of the Management Board of the State Ltd “Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre”; and Lilita Vagale, Chair of the Latvian Trade Union “Enerģija”.
About JSC "Augstsprieguma tīkls"
AST, the Latvian electrical power transmission system operator, ensures uninterrupted and secure transmission of electricity throughout Latvia. Its vision is to become the leading transmission system operator in the region through the efficient and successful implementation of development-oriented changes. AST has 68.46% shareholding in the capital of the operator of the natural gas transmission and storage system JSC “Conexus Baltic Grid”.

Estonian Refugee Council opens office in the occupied Palestinian territory  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:24:10 UTC
23:24:10 KST

Despite the October 2025 ceasefire, humanitarian needs in Gaza and the West Bank remain extremely high. The Estonian Refugee Council has established an official presence in the occupied Palestinian territory to expand its humanitarian assistance and livelihoods programmes.
The new presence will allow ERC to expand its work in both Gaza and the West Bank, with a particular focus on cash-based humanitarian assistance and livelihoods recovery. A permanent presence will enable closer cooperation with local partners, more direct assessment of needs, and faster adaptation of programmes as conditions change.
Eero Janson, Director of the Estonian Refugee Council, said: “We have been working in the occupied Palestinian territory with local partners since autumn 2025. Establishing a permanent presence means that we can now remain engaged at a time when the need for humanitarian assistance has by no means disappeared with the ceasefire. In Gaza, a large share of the population continues to depend on humanitarian assistance, while displacement and protection needs are increasing across the West Bank. Being present locally will allow us to respond more quickly with our partners, reach people whose needs might otherwise remain unmet, and gradually complement emergency assistance with support for people to rebuild their livelihoods.”
Humanitarian needs across the occupied Palestinian territory remain extremely high. While the October 2025 ceasefire and the scale-up of humanitarian assistance have brought measurable improvements in Gaza, these gains remain highly fragile and much of the population continues to depend on external assistance. An estimated 82 per cent of all structures in Gaza have been damaged, while nearly the entire population of 2.1 million people is concentrated in less than half of the Strip. Some 1.4 million people are projected to face Crisis-level or worse acute food insecurity in the second half of 2026; without continued humanitarian food assistance, this figure would rise to an estimated 1.9 million. Hostilities meanwhile continue, including incidents affecting health facilities and other civilian infrastructure. Humanitarian and protection needs are also increasing across the West Bank. Operations by Israeli forces, settler violence, demolitions and movement restrictions continue to drive displacement, undermine livelihoods and restrict access to essential services.
The Estonian Refugee Council has been active in the occupied Palestinian territory since September 2025. Working with a local partner and with support from private donors in Estonia and the Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the organisation provided food assistance to hospitals across the territory. In total, more than 12,000 food parcels were distributed, helping to ensure daily meals for both patients and hospital staff working under extremely challenging conditions.
The Estonian Refugee Council (ERC) is a rights-based humanitarian organisation. Established in 2000, the Estonian Refugee Council has grown to become the largest humanitarian organisation in the Baltics. ERC currently operates in Estonia, Ukraine, Armenia, Syria, Sudan and the occupied Palestinian territory. ERC provides immediate assistance in emergencies and supports crisis-affected people in rebuilding their lives. Donate on the Estonian Refugee Council´s website to help us provide critical aid to those in urgent need.

CENTCOM commander tries to ease concerns about USS Abraham Lincoln
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

23:24:00 KST

CENTCOM commander tries to assuage concerns about USS Abraham Lincoln with visit to carrier
U.S. Central Command Adm. Brad Cooper tried to assuage concerns about the sailors and Marines aboard USS Abraham Lincoln after visiting the aircraft carrier over the weekend.
A number of families have voiced worries that mental health conditions on the ship are deteriorating, and there have been some complaints about sanitary conditions and food supplies during the lengthy deployment amid the U.S.-Iran war. A typical deployment is six months, but the service members aboard the USS Lincoln have been deployed for nine months and counting.
In a statement posted to X, Cooper said deployment at sea is "uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways."
"I've long believed that mental health is another aspect of individual health and requires our attention just like physical health and spiritual health," Cooper added, without confirming or denying any specific issues.
The Military Times and Stars and Stripes recently reported suicide attempts and declining morale among the ship's thousands of sailors and Marines.
Jefferson Kelley, whose son, Jackson, is aboard the Lincoln, told CBS News the service members "should not be deployed this long."
"These are old ships," he told CBS News. "It's not like they're even state-of-the-art. And they take a lot of maintenance, a lot of work. It's around the clock."
A U.S. official previously told CBS News that the USS George Washington aircraft carrier is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, although that may take time.
The Navy has said it has not seen an increase in reported suicidal ideation or suicide attempts on board. An Aug. 3 incident in which a sailor fell overboard and was recovered remain under investigation, the Navy said.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has described reports of the ship's conditions as "completely misrepresented." President Trump also disputed the concerns, saying the Lincoln's deployment has been "not nearly long enough" when asked if the carrier has been deployed too long.
Republicans and Democrats in Congress, however, are demanding answers.
GOP Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska said on Sunday that Congress should conduct oversight of the ship's conditions, calling for testimony from top Navy officials.
"We should have oversight," Bacon said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."

Bruce Springsteen biographer and music critic Dave Marsh dies at 76
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-17
14:23:02 UTC
23:23:02 KST

Bruce Springsteen biographer and music critic Dave Marsh dies at 76
Dave Marsh, a longtime music critic who wrote several influential books about Bruce Springsteen, including the early biography “Born to Run,” has died. He was 76.
Marsh died Friday in Connecticut, his friend Jeffrey St. Clair, a co-editor of the online magazine Counterpunch, told The Associated Press. St. Clair said Marsh had been suffering from a degenerative brain disease for several years. Jim Rotolo, the SiriusXM radio host, announced Marsh’s death on his social media accounts.
Springsteen paid tribute to Marsh in an Instagram post, writing that the loss had left the band “heartbroken.”
“My great friend Dave, with his straight out of Detroit attitude, was a true Rock ‘n’ Roll lifer. He was soulful, intelligent, heartfelt, opinionated, bruising and often fantastically argumentative,” Springsteen wrote. “He deeply believed in what I was trying to accomplish and his lifetime of support meant the world to me.”
Steven Van Zandt also wrote a remembrance on Instagram, writing “he was fearless, relentless, arrogant, everything you’d want in a RocknRoll troublemaker. And by the way, a tremendous writer.”
Marsh was an early champion of Springsteen, writing about him for Creem magazine and penning his first Rolling Stone cover story in 1978. In 1979 his biography “Born to Run: The Bruce Springsteen Story” was released and became a best seller. He followed it in 1986 with “Glory Days: Bruce Springsteen in the 1980s.” Legend has it that he was the one responsible for getting Jon Landau, Springsteen’s longtime manager and record producer, to his first Springsteen concert.
Born in Pontiac, Michigan, in 1950, Marsh dropped out of Detroit’s Wayne State University in 1969 to write for the new rock magazine “Creem,” where Lester Bangs was among his friends and mentors. Springsteen wasn’t Marsh’s only subject, but he was always close by. In 1979, he married Barbara Carr, who would go on to be Springsteen’s co-manager alongside Landau for decades. The rocker even attended their wedding.
He and Carr also devoted much effort to The Kristen Ann Carr Fund, a charity that they started named after their daughter who died from sarcoma at age 21 in 1993. Later that year, Springsteen hosted a benefit concert at Madison Square Garden, where they raised $1.5 million.
Marsh also wrote “The Heart of Rock & Soul: The 1001 Greatest Singles Ever Made,” a biography of The Who, and a book about The Kingsmen hit “Louie Louie.” In recent years he was a frequent co-host and guest on the E Street Nation SiriusXM channel.
___
National Writer Hillel Italie contributed from New York.
