Notes from Central Taiwan: From vaccines to drones: The anatomy of Taiwan’s political forgetting
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:32 UTC
01:41:32 KST

The Tzu Chi Foundation, the globally known Buddhist charity, announced on July 21, 2021 that it had signed a deal to purchase 5 million doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech (BNT) COVID-19 vaccine. It said that the vaccine doses would be donated to the government’s COVID vaccine program. In October the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) made a public announcement thanking the Buddhist foundation and others for the 889,200 doses of the BNT vaccine they had collectively donated.
FRAUD
Earlier this month, the public was stunned to learn that prosecutors had indicted former Changhua Bar Association chairwoman, Chen Yu-hsuan (陳昱瑄), and others on suspicion of defrauding Tzu Chi of over NT$1.06 billion by falsely claiming to have special channels for purchasing BNT vaccines. According to investigators, the suspects had neither the ability nor the means to obtain the vaccine as they had claimed.
Photo courtesy of the Taichung District Prosecutors’ Office via CNA
According to local media, prosecutors said that Tzu Chi had stated that the manufacturer’s quote was US$205 million (US$41 per dose), but Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) and Hon Hai Precision Industry Co (鴻海精密, also known as Foxconn Technology Group, 富士康科技集團), who were also buying and donating vaccines, had a budget of approximately US$175 million (US$36 per dose). The difference was US$30 million, or roughly the equivalent of the NT$1.06 billion commission paid by Tzu Chi to the fraudsters.
The alleged fraudsters, posing as brokers, had apparently inserted themselves into Tzu Chi’s vaccine acquisition program. They told the charity that they could procure the vaccines, took the money on trust and did nothing because the vaccines were coming anyway through other channels. Incredibly, it seems Tzu Chi neither did due diligence when first approached, nor did it follow up to see whether any purchases had taken place on its behalf. It apparently remained completely unaware it had been victimized until investigators stumbled onto the scam while pursuing another case, according to media reports.
This story has blown up as a major political issue, particularly in the Taipei mayoral campaign, as it revisits a past of Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) attacks on the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and its vaccine policies, including accusations of corruption and cronyism. These accusations have gone down the rabbit hole of political forgetting, though they follow the pattern of the KMT whenever the DPP makes a pro-Taiwan move instead of supporting the People’s Republic of China (PRC). That pattern of forgetting is also a feature of the public’s reception of KMT attacks on Taiwan and the DPP.
Photo courtesy of the Changhua County Public Health Bureau
Readers may recall that during 2021 there were numerous donations of vaccines by Japan, the US and other countries. However, as a recent editorial recounts in the Liberty Times (the sister paper of the Taipei Times), political and business figures associated with the KMT and Taiwan People’s Party (TPP), began to promote the German-made BNT vaccine. The apparent attention of this program was to stop the use of any vaccines but BNT.
However, the “Greater China” distribution rights for BNT vaccine were obtained by Shanghai-based Fosun Group (復星國際). Though Taiwan secured a contract for 5 million doses of BNT in early 2021, the PRC halted the sale. (It is astonishing that the repeated betrayals of local KMT interests by the PRC never affects KMT willingness to support the PRC.)
To fill in the gap, private organizations stepped in. However, as the government observed at the time, private groups cannot bear the legal and compensation responsibilities if health problems with the vaccines should arise. Hence, the vaccines had to be given to the government. Private groups had to obtain government authorization and a special import permit to bring in vaccines. Because of these requirements, former Minister of Health and Welfare and then-head of the Central Epidemic Command Center, Chen Shih-chung (陳時中), a DPP appointee, repeatedly reminded these organizations that brokers who claimed to have procurement channels were likely scammers.
Photo: Fang Pin-chao, Taipei Times
Politicians from the KMT and TPP camps attacked the DPP for “blocking vaccines” and killing Taiwanese. The Liberty Times recalled that then-chairman of the TPP, Ko Wen-je (柯文哲), said that “at the height of the pandemic, the government blocked BNT from entering the country in order to ‘protect high-end vaccines.’”
Indeed, Johnny Chiang (江啟臣), then-chairman of the KMT, sued Chen Shi-chung and the director of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for corruption, saying that they had profited from these high-end vaccines. The KMT also accused the DPP of using dangerous, untested vaccines on young people, since older people had priority for vaccines. As Brian Hioe pointed out at Taiwan Insight, the KMT was “hoping to make inroads with a demographic that has drifted away” from the party. The KMT also attacked the Astra-Zeneca vaccine, though major figures in the KMT quietly had themselves vaccinated with it.
Chiang’s complaints follow the typical pattern of KMT attacks. Chiang said that the KMT had always supported the development of domestically produced vaccines, but it supports “safe and effective” vaccines that adhere to international standards and acquire international certification, not vaccines whose growth is artificially accelerated.
Photo: Tu Chien-jung, Taipei Times
DRONES
Sound familiar? Just substitute the word “drones” for “vaccines.” The KMT has one pattern of attack, which it always uses: accuse the DPP of corruption whenever it is doing something Taiwan-centered, say that the DPP approach is too expensive, while simultaneously putting its hand on its heart and piously proclaiming that it has always supported whatever program it is attacking. The last two decades offer many examples of this playbook.
For then-legislator and current Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安), the vaccine issue became an important line of attack on the DPP. He said the DPP was “constantly blocking vaccines and protecting high-end vaccines,” and asked the public: “Do you believe Tzu Chi or the DPP?”, as if the two were in conflict.
The pro-China parties’ attack on the DPP thus accused it of killing people to make money for vaccine makers it was connected to, which the Liberty Times said had powerful effects on the 2022 local elections. The attacks continued into 2023, as a recent Taipei Times editorial observed, impacting the 2024 elections. A legislator at the time, Chiang Wan-an sat in on closed meetings on government vaccine procurement, and knew what was really going on.
As the Liberty Times pointed out, this was the same playbook that Chiang is now using in the tainted oil failure of the Taipei and Taichung city governments — accusing the central government of forcing people to consume toxic oil, when in fact KMT-led governments were responsible.
The brazen fraud against Tzu Chi has completely destroyed Chiang’s accusations from the COVID era and vindicated Chen Shi-chung’s warnings about fraud. DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) has had a field day accusing Chiang Wan-an of hypocrisy and lies. A CMmedia piece last week said that the DPP hopes to use the KMT’s now-exposed vaccine attacks as leverage in the elections in Taipei, Hsinchu and Nantou.
Hopefully voters will finally make the connection between drones, tainted oil, vaccines and a hundred other items.
KMT politicians just this week were complaining that the public should have been better informed about the Internet slow down drills. KMT Legislator Ko Ju-chun (葛如鈞) said without better clarity the drills were essentially treating the public as “guinea pigs.”
Sound familiar?

Heat, water scarcity driving stranded-asset risks: report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:30 UTC
01:41:30 KST

Extreme heat and unreliable water supplies are threatening asset valuations across a growing number of sectors as everything from labor productivity to energy costs gets impacted, an analysis by Moody’s released on Friday showed.
“Heat and water are no longer separate perils moving on separate timelines,” Moody’s managing director and head of catastrophe modeling for insurance solutions Mohsen Rahnama said. “They are converging, and doing so quickly.”
For investors, “both perils translate into operational risk, earnings volatility and stranded-asset exposure,” he said.
Photo: Bloomberg
This year is on track to be the hottest recorded in human history. In Europe, the fastest-warming continent, heat has exposed huge gaps in the region’s preparedness as its infrastructure buckles. Economists are already warning that disruptions to harvests, commodity supplies and the ability of humans to function would hit inflation and GDP.
Heat and water risk are starting to “weigh on values” in the real estate sector, Rahnama said.
Such impacts, left unpriced, “can quietly erode cash flows and portfolio returns” for firms in sectors spanning agriculture, the manufacture of apparel and of semiconductors, he said.
The upshot is that investors need to adapt to a “new risk landscape” created by extreme weather conditions, as the impact of heat and water scarcity morph into permanent risk features, Rahnama said.
“Reinsurers, banks and investors are watching these same trends closely, given their reach across regions and their role in how capital moves in response to physical risk,” he said.
In the US, Moody’s said a sample of about 159,000 water-intensive facilities revealed that close to 49,000 might face high or very high water stress in the decades ahead.
Most are concentrated in Texas and California, while more than 60 percent of the facilities reviewed are used for heavy manufacturing and processing.
About one-quarter are used for producing food and drinks, while 14 percent are for mining and quarrying, the report said.
Such risks can be hard for insurers to capture, due to the slow-moving nature of the damage done.
“Traditional indemnity cover sits awkwardly with chronic risk,” Rahnama said.
However, “losses from heat and water stress build slowly, are hard to model precisely, and tend to strike many policyholders in a region at once, overwhelming the usual diversification,” he said.

A Chinese container vessel has set sail for Europe through the arctic, part of new weekly service on a route that cuts shipment times in half but which environmental groups warn could speed up the melting of polar ice.
The Dubai Tower left the eastern port city of Ningbo, China, on Saturday evening heading north, where it would pass through the Bering Strait, then turn west through the frigid waters along Russia’s northern coast.
It is expected to reach Felixstowe in the UK on Sept. 7, followed by stops in Hamburg, Germany, and Gdynia, Poland, later that week, a timetable published by Sea Legend showed.
Photo: AFP
The Northern Sea Route (NSR) from China to Europe is significantly faster than that through the Suez Canal and allows vessels to avoid the Red Sea, where shipping has been targeted by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
However, the route is only accessible during the time of the year when the ice is melted enough.
Global shipping is heavily disrupted by war in the Middle East.
Other shipping companies have transited the arctic passage before, with Denmark’s Maersk the first to do so in 2018.
Last year, 23 container ships transited through, up from 15 in 2024, a shipping analysis from business insurer Allianz Commercial showed.
Environmental groups warn that increasing numbers of ships transiting the shorter NSR could accelerate loss of arctic sea ice — already made vulnerable by rising global temperatures.
Major shipping companies including France’s CMA CGM, Switzerland-headquartered MSC and Germany-based Hapag-Lloyd have pledged to “avoid arctic trans-shipment routes.”
However, analysts say the arctic could serve as an important future trade route, particularly for China, which has outlined plans for greater access to the region through a “polar Silk Road.”

Belgium battling record wildfire, evacuating people
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:25 UTC
01:41:25 KST

Hundreds of villagers were on Saturday under evacuation orders in eastern Belgium as firefighters battled one of the country’s worst-ever wildfires, with vast swathes of nature reserve turned to a singed wasteland.
Reinforcements were pulled from across the country to fight the blaze that broke out on Friday in the High Fens park near the German border and quickly spread, with helicopters and water bombers flying in from across the EU to help.
Described by officials as the largest in Belgium’s modern history, the blaze broke out in an area of fragile peatlands and pine forests that was ravaged by massive wildfires in 1911, during a similar period of extreme heatwaves and drought.
Photo: AFP
By late on Saturday, it had scorched more than 2,700 hectares, up from a mere 80 hectares on Friday, the local authorities said in a statement. “You can’t see a thing anymore, there’s smoke everywhere,” said David Rodolfs, a restaurant owner in the nearby Waimes area.
Rodolfs said his colleagues witnessed the fire breaking out on Friday.
“There was ash falling onto the tables, and then we asked our customers to leave. No dessert, everyone had to go,” the 38-year-old said.
The authorities warned that the rugged nature of the region’s terrain was “preventing the emergency services from tackling the fire at close quarters ... using their usual methods”.
Residents in parts of the nearby villages of Sourbrodt and Buetgenbach were on Saturday ordered to evacuate afternoon as a precautionary measure, the authorities said.
The Belga news agency reported that 600 people were told to leave. A gymnasium in the neighboring municipality of Malmedy was opened up to offer shelter.
“We are here to provide them with information and meet their basic needs; that is, food, water and somewhere to rest, particularly for the most vulnerable people,” the Belgian Red Cross’ Romane Bouhaben said.
Others in the area were advised to remain indoors, and keep doors and windows closed.
Nicolas Yernaux, a spokesperson for the regional authorities in Wallonia, said that the fire was not under control.
“There is a risk that the fire could reach homes, but we are deploying all available resources to protect them,” Yernaux said.
A huge expanse of blackened vegetation was visible in the burn zone with thick yellow smoke hanging in the air.
Belgium swiftly activated the EU’s civil protection mechanism, allowing it to request personnel and equipment from across the continent. A Dutch helicopter was already on site, with two more on the way along with two Swedish water-bombing aircraft.
“They will be operational from tomorrow,” European Commissioner for Humanitarian Aid and Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib said, calling the blaze the latest sign of the “climate upheaval” affecting the continent.
“Never before has the wildfire season started so early in the year and reached such northern latitudes,” she said.
Operations were being made harder by the fens’ terrain — a patchwork of heath, peat bogs and raised wooden boardwalks.
Firefighters had “pulled back to the edge of the forest and allowed parts of the heathland to burn, because the area is very difficult to access,” Yernaux said.
“The situation is complicated and highly dependent on aerial resources,” he added.

Businessman talks of TAO’s indifference
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:23 UTC
01:41:23 KST

Former Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers’ Association (TEEMA) chairman Richard Wu (吳思鍾) yesterday called for suspension of cross-strait exchanges, accusing China’s Taiwan Affairs Office (TAO) Director Song Tao (宋濤) of mistreating Taiwanese businesses.
Wu, chairman of the Kingtel Communication Corp (西陵電子), made the remarks in an interview with the Liberty Times (sister paper of the Taipei Times) as he saying he was cheated out of a major investment in China.
Wu says he has spent 25 years seeking justice after relatives of senior Chinese Communist Party officials cheated him out of his investment in a project in Beijing.
Photo: Liao Chia-ning, Taipei Times
Wu said that his joint venture in Beijing, which involved a property of 40,000 ping (about 132,000 square meters) seized by a corrupt group associated with former Chinese public security minister Zhou Yongkang (周永康) and relatives of other officials.
“I won the lawsuit, but neither I nor the 1,650 shareholders have received a cent in compensation to this day,” he said. “The Chinese judicial system has treated the people of Taiwan unfairly and unjustly.”
Wu said he had sought assistance through various channels, including raising the matter with Chinese authorities through Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文). However, Song ignored the issue and refused to forward a letter Wu had written seeking help from Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平), he said.
Wu said Song is the least concerned with victimized Taiwanese businesspeople of all the directors of the TAO.
He said previous directors such as Chen Yunlin (陳雲林) and Zhang Zhijun (張志軍) paid more attention to complaints brought by Taiwanese businesspeople. Before 2016, he said, the TAO’s Coordination Bureau sent officials to Taiwan every three months to review the progress of cases involving Taiwanese businesspeople with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs.
However, the governments on both sides of the Taiwan Strait have stopped official exchanges since 2016, he said. Many Taiwanese businesspeople who have encountered misdealings in China have sought assistance from the KMT, the Taiwan People’s Party and the Taiwan Statebuilding Party through their channels with the TAO, he said, adding that while former Taiwan Affairs Office director Liu Jieyi (劉結一) expressed concern publicly, he took no action.
Wu called on all groups and organizations in Taiwan, including the KMT, to raise the issue of challenges faced by Taiwanese businesspeople in China with officials in Beijing.
“China’s judicial system must treat the people of Taiwan fairly,” he said. “If the TAO refuses to address the persecution of Taiwanese businesspeople and people from Taiwan in China, we should suspend cross-strait exchanges.”
Wu said that he does not support Taiwan independence and has advocated peaceful, equal exchanges between Taiwan and China. Song is unfit for the position of TAO director because he believes Taiwanese businesspeople are easily bullied in China, Wu said.
Cross-strait exchanges are not something China bestows on Taiwan, he added.
When reached for comment, Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Legislator Chen Pei-yu (陳培瑜) yesterday said Wu’s experience should be taken seriously by everyone who advocates for greater cross-strait exchanges, adding that the most basic prerequisite for such exchanges is ensuring the safety, property and basic rights of Taiwanese.
Chen said the issue has gone beyond the usual blue-versus-green political divide.
Chen said that she questioned the TAO’s repeated calls for greater exchanges, integration and support for Taiwanese people.
“If Taiwanese businesspeople receive no meaningful assistance when they are mistreated and need help, it raises the question of how such exchanges could make people in Taiwan feel secure,” she said.
Chen urged the KMT, which advocates closer cross-strait ties, to take the matter seriously.
With a Taiwanese businessperson publicly appealing for help, she asked whether the KMT was willing to step forward and demand that the Chinese government provide an explanation.
No response from the KMT was available at press time.

Time zone switch debate resurfaces online
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:22 UTC
01:41:22 KST

An online debate has resurfaced on whether Taiwan should switch to the same time zone as Japan, with supporters citing its geographic location and saying that China would have no right to object.
The debate erupted on Threads when users suggested that Taiwan should stop using the same time zone as China, Malaysia and Singapore, GMT+8, and instead switch one hour ahead to the same time zone as Japan and South Korea, GMT+9, which it is geographically closer to.
Under GMT+9 the sun would set later year-round, meaning that people would see sunlight after getting off work even in the winter and feel less weary, users said.
Photo: Screen grab from Wikipedia
More than half of the world’s countries have time zones that do not align with their geographic longitude, for reasons including sovereignty claims, colonial history, centralized governance, daylight hours and cross-border trade, a user said.
In addition, each country’s time zone is considered a matter of national sovereignty, as there is no global authority that regulates time zones, so each country can set its own time zone according to its needs, they said.
However, others said that it is long working hours that are the cause of burnout and weariness among workers, not the time zone.
Instead, the government should promote flexible or shorter working hours, with optional overtime, as 9am to 6pm is too long for a normal workday, they said.
Many supporters of changing the time zone said Taiwan feels more closely aligned with Japan and that having a different time zone than China would underscore that the two are not subordinate to each other.
Others said there was little reason for Taiwan to share China’s time zone when it does not follow China’s government or market hours.
Taiwan uses GMT+8 largely because the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) government brought the system with it when it fled to Taiwan following its defeat by the Chinese Communist Party.
The time zone was called Chungyuan Standard Time and was established in the early days of the Republic of China based on the global standard time for the 120th meridian east longitude.
According to National Archives Administration records, during the Japanese colonial period, Taiwan adopted the same standard time as Japan beginning in 1937, due to Japan’s military needs and its policy of further integrating Taiwan with the Japanese mainland.
After Japan’s defeat in World War II in 1945, it ended the use of Japan’s Central Standard Time in Taiwan and the KMT government incorporated Taiwan into Chungyuan Standard Time, records from Taiwan Historica show.
After Taiwan’s first change of ruling party in 2000, the administration of then-president Chen Shui-bian (陳水扁) renamed Chungyuan Standard Time to National Standard Time.

The Detroit Tigers’ Taiwanese infielder Lee Hao-yu on Saturday recorded his 54th hit of the season in his first at-bat against the Chicago White Sox, matching Yu Chang for the most hits in a single season by a Taiwanese MLB player.

Lee, who started the game at third base, also played a major defensive role in a crucial double play in the top of the second inning.
Photo: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images
With runners on first and second, Tigers starter Troy Melton fielded a ground ball bunted by Jake Rogers and tossed it to Lee, who forced out Chase Meidroth at third before throwing to second base to also get Tristan Peters out.
Lee went 1-for-3. He has a batting average of .266 for the season.
The Tigers ultimately lost 4-3, their second consecutive defeat. Chicago (64-58) have won five of their past seven games and lead the American League Central, ahead of the Tigers (60-63) and the Minnesota Twins (60-64).
Photo: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images
The single-season record of 54 hits was previously held solely by former MLB infielder Chang, who reached the mark in 2021 while playing for the then-Cleveland Indians.
Chang reached 54 hits in 237 at-bats over 89 games, while Lee tied the record in just 203 at-bats in 78 games.

Photo: AP
In Chicago, Joshua Baez sent the first pitch he saw in the majors about 137m for a home run, then homered in his next two at-bats to become the first player to go deep in each of his first three MLB at-bats, leading the St Louis Cardinals to an 8-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Baez flashed a grin to the St Louis dugout as he began his home run trot.
“There was a calmness and a smile, like, ‘I’m here,’” Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said. “It’s rare for me to pick my head up to enjoy parts of it. He didn’t exactly give us an option, but to actually take a step back and enjoy the heck out of what was going on there.”
Called up from Triple-A Memphis before the game, Baez had 30 members of his family in attendance at Wrigley Field. The traveling party, which included his mother, Yris Baez, gathered on the field for photos afterward in spite of rain.

MLB said Baez was the first player in modern baseball history to hit three home runs in his debut. The league cannot say with certainty whether the feat happened before 1901 due to a lack of game logs.

The two superstars had already faced off twice, with Misiorowski throwing six straight fastballs over 164kph to retire him on a popup leading off the game.

CPC Corp, Taiwan (CPC, 台灣中油) on Saturday announced that it would keep retail gasoline and diesel prices unchanged this week, and Formosa Petrochemical Corp (台塑石化) followed suit yesterday.
The decisions marked the third consecutive week that CPC and Formosa have kept their domestic fuel prices steady despite a rise in crude oil prices last week, amid no signs of progress toward reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
CPC said its floating price mechanism, based on a weighted average of 70 percent Dubai crude and 30 percent Brent crude, showed that the average international crude oil price rose to US$89.84 last week from US$82.20 per barrel the previous week, with no immediate signs of a peace agreement between the US and Iran.
A stronger New Taiwan dollar, which the US dollar averaging NT$32.194 last week, compared with NT$32.350 a week earlier, helped CPC offset the rise in crude oil prices to some extent, it said.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16

Australian Lani Pallister on Saturday dealt US great Katie Ledecky her first 800m freestyle defeat in a major international meet, beating her one-time idol at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships in Irvine, California.
Pallister led wire-to-wire on the way to victory in 8 minuts, 06.10 seconds and Ledecky’s desperate late charge was not enough as she finished second in 8:07.26.
It was a stunning result on the final day of Pan Pacs action that saw American Kate Douglass break the 50m freestyle world record twice on the way to gold and earn 200m breaststroke silver and medley relay gold as well.
Photo: AP
Ledecky has dominated the 800m since she won Olympic gold in 2012 as a 15-year-old, winning 13 international golds since then. That includes four Olympic gold medals and seven world titles in the event.
Pallister, who claimed her first career win over Ledecky in the 400m free earlier this week before finishing second behind her in the 1,500m, showed that rule can be broken as the 29-year-old American looks to add to her collection of nine Olympic gold medals at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
The Australian punched the water in delight and got a hug across the lane rope from Ledecky.
“Katie is such a dominant force,” said Pallister, who finished the week with gold in the 200, 400 and 800m free and the 4x200m free relay. “Without her, we wouldn’t have women’s distance swimming in the place we’re at at the moment. To be part of that story at the moment [it’s] pretty much all because we get to chase Katie.”
Meanwhile, Douglass firmly established herself as the one to chase in the 50m free, winning the final in a devastating 23.19 seconds.
That sliced three-tenths of a second off the world record of 23.49 seconds she set hours earlier and saw her finish 55-hundredths of a second ahead of US teammate Gretchen Walsh.
Walsh had set a world record of 23.55 on June 28 in Rome — where she broke the world mark Douglass had set on June 19.

Corgis race, bark and sniff their way to glory
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:15 UTC
01:41:15 KST

It is not all about short-legged speed when 150 corgis gather for an international race celebrating the little dogs. There is a costume parade, the “smartest nose” and — of course — the loudest bark.
The fifth Corgi Race Vilnius drew dogs and their owners to the Lithuanian capital’s Vingis park on Saturday for what organizers said was the biggest edition yet.
There were competitors from Lithuania, Latvia, Poland, Estonia, Germany, Ukraine, the Czech Republic, the US and the UK — which is most closely associated with the breed, famously a favorite of the late Queen Elizabeth II.
Photo: AP
“In the first year, we gathered 40 corgis from one city. This year, it’s 150 from nine countries, and for the first time we have a participant from the place where the breed originated,” organizer Edvinas Miskas said. “We call Vilnius the European capital of corgis, and when people from the breed’s homeland start coming to us rather than the other way around, that title begins to sound a little more serious.”
Ninety-four dogs took part in the main running event, competing in qualifiers, semi-finals and the final.
In the final, which pitted corgis against each other over 25m, the winner was American competitor GG, short for Gustave the Girl Dog. Another US entrant, Mr Corgington, finished a close second. Lithuania’s own Moka, a two-time former champion, was third.
Much of the program dispensed with speed to explore the other skills of the dogs — and their owners.
There was a costume parade featuring 38 corgis in diverse outfits including a dinosaur suit, a dress and doggy sports gear. Amigo swept both the four-judge jury and the public Facebook vote for a flawless costume entry with a knight-like look.
In the “smartest nose” challenge, dogs searched for hidden treats. Latvian corgis Tora and Rusty shared the win.
The first British competitor, 12-year-old Pembroke Welsh corgi Duke from Sedbergh in northwest England, did not participate in the main race because of his stately age, but was a hopeful in the barking stakes after, as his owner put it, training for his whole life.
However, it was Mr Corgington who won the loudest bark contest.
He was one of the most traveled competitors. The final race offered him a rematch after he finished second against GG at a major race at Emerald Downs in Auburn, Washington — her second consecutive win there.
Half of the corgis registered in Vilnius this year were competing for the first time, but six veterans — costume winner Amigo, Foksas, Foksis, Madeira, Bulka and Dziugas — have attended every edition.

Thousands await aid after deadly Indonesian quake
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:12 UTC
01:41:12 KST

Help could not come soon enough on yesterday for thousands of evacuees on Indonesia’s Flores island after a powerful earthquake killed at least 53 people, injured dozens and damaged hundreds of houses and buildings.
About 5,000 people fled their homes as the magnitude 7.7 quake hit the island early on Saturday, followed by about 1,000 aftershocks of varying intensities in the hours that followed, officials said.
People in some areas were left without electricity and telecommunications, and at least one emergency access road remained inaccessible.
Photo: AP
“We need food, drink, medicines and diapers for the children,” Umri, a resident of Nangahale village on the north coast of Flores, said yesterday morning.
The 55-year-old, who like many Indonesians uses one name, has been hiding out on a hilltop for 24 hours with others afraid to return home.
At Kisol village a few hours away, Bertolomeus Tiga, 42, said that his house was one of several collapsed by the quake that also brought down part of the local church.
“The police came yesterday and collected all the data, but there’s no aid yet. The most important thing is probably staple foods. Food and drink ... medicine,” he said.
Bertolomeus said villagers were afraid to return to compromised homes and buildings.
“For the time being, we’re still taking refuge outside. We’re still living outside,” he added.
The head of the Indonesian National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB), Suharyanto, said at least five helicopters, several planes, a naval vessel and search and rescue ships were on their way to help.
The agency upped the death toll yesterday to 53 from 47 the day before, with 135 people injured.
There were no reports of missing people.
Survivors were in urgent need of assistance in the form of emergency tents, food, medicines, blankets, camp beds, mats, clean water and electricity generators, rescue officials said.
The epicenter of the shallow quake was located just off the north coast of the island, authorities said.
The affected areas have few, if any, high-rise buildings.
BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan said at least 914 houses on the island were severely damaged and hundreds of others to a lesser degree.
Dozens of public buildings were also affected, including 93 educational and 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said on Saturday that preparations were under way to bring aid to thousands in temporary shelters.
The Indonesian government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc’s Copernicus Earth observation satellites.
In Ruteng, a town about 200km from the worst-hit part of the island, heavy machinery were clearing rubble from the street yesterday.
The local hospital had been badly damaged, and patients were evacuated to tents erected outside.

ITRI develops tech therapy for anxiety
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:11 UTC
01:41:11 KST

The Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) has developed Taiwan’s first digital therapeutic technology for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), which combines noninvasive micro-electrical stimulation of the vagus nerve through the ear with physiological data analysis.
The Taiwan-based applied research and technology development organization said it aims to offer an alternative treatment option to medication for GAD and is applying for clinical trials, with the goal of being practically applied within three to five years.
A study by the Ministry of Health and Welfare showed that 25 to 27 percent of people in Taiwan experience psychological stress, said Hu Chang-lin (胡長霖), a project manager at ITRI’s Biomedical Technology and Device Research Laboratories.
Photo courtesy of the institute
More than 2 million people have sought medical attention because of mental illness, but only 1 to 7 percent paid for mental health treatment using the National Health Insurance system, Hu said.
“There remains a significant unmet need for treatment,” he said.
Most psychological diseases are treated with medication, but long-term use could generate side effects, dependence and tolerance, Hu said.
As many people with anxiety disorders are often reluctant to seek medical help, a significant number miss the optimal window for treatment, he added.
The therapeutic technology was developed to provide a third treatment option for GAD beyond medication and psychotherapy, Hu said, adding that the technology could potentially help patients gradually reduce their reliance on drugs.
People with anxiety disorders often experience an imbalance in autonomic nervous system regulation, characterized by heightened sympathetic nervous activity and reduced parasympathetic activity, Hu said.
They can remain in a prolonged state of tension and worry and have difficulty relaxing, he said.
The device developed by ITRI stimulates the vagus nerve through the ear, activating the parasympathetic nervous system, Hu said.
This not only helps relieve emotional distress, but can also influence emotional regulation areas of the brain, including the brainstem and prefrontal cortex, through neural signaling, improving patients’ ability to regulate their emotions, he added.
Although non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation (nVNS) technology has been in development in North America and Europe for years, most products are only equipped with the function of unidirectional electrical stimulation, Hu said.
No nVNS-related products have received regulatory approval for marketing in Taiwan, Hu said.
The key breakthrough achieved by the ITRI-developed technology platform is to integrate heart rate variability (HRV), photoplethysmography and other physiological signal measurements. Data can be uploaded to the cloud for doctors to conduct real-time analyses, he said.
Users can also use the device to monitor patients’ biodata before the clinic visits and help doctors produce more accurate diagnoses, he said.
The institute is applying for a clinical trial for the device, and the application review could take up to 1.5 years, he said.
“We hope that this device can be purchased at an affordable price to facilitate home-based care for more patients,” Hu said.

MOE to expand first aid training to school faculty
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:09 UTC
01:41:09 KST

The Ministry of Education is to expand the emergency medical technician (EMT) training from nurses to faculty and staff at schools to boost on-campus emergency medical services capacity, ministry official said last week.
The emergency rescue golden hour for a student who has passed out or been injured, or for a mass casualty incident on campus depends on proper first aid responses.
The ministry has required school nurses to complete at least 40 hours of EMT training and is expanding the program to school faculty and staff, who would receive EMT-1, the basic level of training, to build a larger frontline emergency response workforce, the MOE said.
Photo courtesy of the Ministry of Education
K-12 Education Administration official Chiu Chiu-chan (邱秋嬋) said that school nurses must receive at least 40 hours of EMT training in accordance with the ministry’s guidelines for emergency injury treatment in schools.
The goal of the policy is not just to increase the number of trainees earning a certificate, but to enable proper and independent first aid treatments when emergencies occur in schools, she said.
That helps secure more golden time for emergency rescue, Chiu said, adding that there were a total of 77 school nurses, faculty and staff from primary or secondary schools participating in the EMT-1 training.
The administration has been promoting the EMT-1 training since 2024 and commissioned the National Academy for Educational Research to organize training programs, she said.
Professional fire and emergency medical knowledge was also integrated into these programs, Chiu said.
The ministry expects such systemic and standardized training programs to help form a campus emergency response support network, she said.
The EMT-1 training was last year extended from nurses to faculty and staff so that schools would have more people to provide assistance when needed, she added.
Campus safety is the foundation of education, Chiu said.
The ministry would continue to integrate professional resources regarding fire safety, healthcare and education to advance first aid treatment trainings and increase on-campus security resilience, she said.
The EMT-1 training program comprises 56 hours.
It includes adult and pediatric cardiopulmonary resuscitation, automated external defibrillator use, cervical spine immobilization, mass-casualty triage, trauma bleeding control and bandaging, management of common medical emergencies and injuries, and infectious disease prevention and control.
It also includes scenario-based training in on-site decisionmaking and team response.
Trainees who complete the program must pass the written and practical examinations to obtain EMT-1 certification.

BOOKMAN BILINGUAL 雙語書林： Chinglish or Natural English? 中式英語或道地英語？
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:06 UTC
01:41:06 KST

1. 太陽一出來，我們就起床。
ˇ As soon as the sun rose, we got up.
χ As soon as the sun raised, we got up.
Photo: AdobeStock l 圖片:AdobeStock
註︰rise, rose, risen 是不及物動詞；raise, raised, raised 是及物動詞，例如：to raise one’s hand。
2. 這次經驗在我心中留下深刻印象。
ˇ This experience has left a deep impression on my mind.
χ This experience has remained a deep impression on my mind.
註︰rise, rose, risen 是不及物動詞；remain 是不及物動詞，有「留下」、「仍是」等意義。例如：
The rest had gone home; he alone remained.
All things remained the same.
「留下印象」是 to leave an impression on 或 to give an impression。
3. 他一天到晚穿著一件皮夾克。
ˇ He wore a leather jacket all day.
ˇ He had a leather jacket on all day.
χ He put on a leather jacket all day.
註︰put on 指「穿上（衣服、鞋子等）」、「戴上（眼鏡、手套等）」，表示一時、瞬間（point of time）的動作。例如：
He put on a leather jacket before he went out.
wear 指「穿著」、「戴著」，表示繼續的動作或狀態。例如：
Most people wear ready-made shoes.
He wore a tailor-made suit.
She wore dark-blue overalls.
4. 我上星期六帶妹妹去看電影。
ˇ I took my sister to the movies last Saturday.
χ I brought my sister to the movies last Saturday.
註︰bring 是「拿來」或「帶來」；take 是「拿去」或「帶去」，或不指明方向。
例如：
Take this empty bottle away and bring me a full one, please.
Bring your younger brother with you next time you come.
When you come to class, bring your dictionary with you, please.
5. 在你來以前我正在找原子筆。
ˇ I was looking for a ballpoint pen before you arrived.
ˇ I was trying to find a ballpoint pen before you arrived.
χ I was finding a ball pen before you came.
註︰find 作「發現」或「找到」解，是瞬間動詞（point-of-time verb），或稱終止動詞（terminative verb），通常不可用進行式。「找尋」應用 to look for 或 to try to find。
Exercises:
A. 他整天穿著笨重的鞋子。
He __________ clumsy, heavy shoes all day.
1. put on
2. wore
3. had on
4. wore on
B. 他在出門前穿上一件毛衣。
He __________ a sweater before he went out.
Answers: A. 2 B. 1

US to tell partners they must pick sides
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:06 UTC
01:41:06 KST

The US is preparing to tell dozens of countries they must pick sides in the artificial intelligence (AI) race with China, warning they would be excluded from a US-led AI coalition if they also sign up for Beijing’s competing framework, according to a US official and an internal draft reviewed by Reuters.
Washington last year launched the Pax Silica initiative aimed at securing supply chains for AI models, semiconductors and critical minerals, amid a fierce technology rivalry with Beijing. About two dozen countries have joined, including Kazakhstan, a key potential source of critical minerals that has also joined China’s coalition, as well as close US allies such as Japan, Australia and South Korea.
The draft letter, prepared by the US Department of State, is addressed to the 35 signatories of a US “AI Opportunity Statement” signed in June, which includes members of the nonbinding Pax Silica framework and other countries that have expressed a desire to align cooperation on AI with Washington.
Photo: AFP
By pressing countries to choose sides the US hopes to starve China of resources in a race to make the most sophisticated AI, which could be used for military or economic dominance.
Last month, Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) launched the “World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization,” promoting his country’s open-weight technology as a challenge to US influence over the fast-moving sector. Kazakhstan is the only country so far known to have joined both initiatives, setting off alarm bells in Washington.
“To be part of everything is to be part of nothing. Signature of the Pax Silica Declaration is not merely a membership subscription, but a commitment,” the letter says, urging countries to “choose deliberately” on AI.
“It cannot be held alongside membership in duplicative initiatives whose expectations conflict with our own,” the letter said, without specifically mentioning China.
The draft was undated. The State Department said it would not comment on “purportedly leaked internal documents.”
The Chinese embassy in Washington said the country opposes politicizing trade and technology issues.
“Such actions will only stifle global AI advances and serve no one’s interests,” an embassy spokesperson said.
The Kazakh embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.
The Pax Silica agreement aims to push US allies and partners toward joint projects and export controls, and ultimately reduce reliance on adversaries for critical minerals, AI models and the semiconductor chips that power them.
The race between the US and China for technological leadership has reached a pivotal moment, as Chinese open-weight AI models have made rapid gains against proprietary systems from US companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic PBC. The exponential growth of the technology’s capabilities, including the ability to hack autonomously, has forced a global reckoning over its power.
Beijing is weighing restrictions on overseas access to some of China’s leading AI models, highlighting the growing tension with its stringent national security agenda.
The US touted Kazakhstan in June as the first country in Central Asia to join Pax Silica, bringing significant reserves of critical minerals that fuel advanced technologies.
China has used its near-monopolies over critical minerals as a retaliatory weapon in a tariff war launched last year by US President Donald Trump, who has ramped up US efforts to source the minerals domestically and from allies.
Members of Pax Silica have access to shared investment opportunities in AI-related projects, while those who sign the AI Opportunity Statement have symbolically agreed on a “common purpose” and “shared vision” with the US, according to the statement posted on the State Department’s Web site.
US officials drafted the letter to make clear that “you can’t have it both ways,” the US official said, speaking on condition of anonymity given ongoing internal discussions on the issue.
“It’s difficult to see how a country can credibly position themselves as trusted partners in one technology ecosystem while simultaneously signing up for an initiative designed by China to advance a competing vision for AI,” the official said.

EDITORIAL: Budget’s passage very unimpressive
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:05 UTC
01:41:05 KST

The Legislative Yuan on Friday finally passed the long-delayed third reading of this year’s central government general budget, setting a new record for the tardiest passage of a general budget — delayed 266 days past the legal deadline, almost running headlong into the next year’s proposed general budget, typically submitted for review before September.
It passed with an overall NT$48 billion (US$1.54 billion) cut across agencies and freezes in spending, including the premier’s salary. It also contained a dramatic twist as the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) suddenly withdrew its proposal to cut the Executive Yuan’s entire six-year, NT$44.2 billion Uncrewed Vehicle Industry Development Program along with other agencies’ drone procurement funding, allowing them to pass. The result drew mixed responses.
The KMT hailed its “compromise” as a gesture of “great goodwill” and claimed it supports domestic drone industry development by passing the funding. The ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and government officials expressed concern over deep cuts and freezes in funding that might critically affect agencies’ operations, as well as over the special budget bill for funding military drones still being blocked by opposition lawmakers.
According to the Budget Act (預算法), the Legislative Yuan should have approved the Executive Yuan’s general budget proposal “a month before the beginning of a new fiscal year,” meaning the review deadline should have been the end of November last year. Local media said that the opposition-controlled Legislative Yuan had strung the budget review along for 350 days since the Cabinet submitted the proposed budget to the legislature last year.
Finally passing the general budget should be good news, even though it happened almost two-thirds of the way through the fiscal year, but opposition lawmakers do not deserve praise for their abrogation of duty or their self-proclaimed “leniency.” Scrutiny on legislators should be increased to hold them accountable.
The KMT, on the last day of the budget review, abruptly withdrew its objections and approved the government’s proposed NT$6.34 billion budget for domestic drone development — as well as the NT$44.2 billion industry development budget overseen by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the NT$19.2 billion budget for various agencies’ drone procurement.
The KMT claimed it was because it “strongly supports Taiwan’s security and the autonomous development of its defense industry,” but the sudden reversal of this important bill highlights the sloppiness and inconsistency of its decisionmaking.
The hasty decision validates speculation that the opposition’s cuts and freezes were not ever based on rational or professional oversight, but were made for political maneuvering and retaliation, with the ultimate goal of disrupting and paralyzing the smooth operation of the government. It is underpinned by the same “cut-and-paste” methods that KMT lawmakers have used to gut funding across government agencies, highlighting their laziness in even pretending to perform their duty reviewing the agency budgets in detail.
The opposition lawmakers’ efforts to disrupt the government’s operation have been a recurring theme since they took up their posts two years ago, demonstrated by their efforts to paralyze the Constitutional Court after it found their legislative power expansion bills unconstitutional, hamstring last year’s budget, and reject almost all judicial nominees, Control Yuan members and agencies that perform public oversight on legislators or on political parties.
During the rushed passage of the general budget last week, the KMT lawmakers’ decisionmaking mechanism raises more serious concerns.
Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜) of the KMT lost his temper in a cross-caucus negotiation on Tuesday last week, saying that KMT caucus whip Fu Kun-chi should either attend the meetings, authorize his colleagues to represent him or resign from his position. It shows that only a few lawmakers, or possibly only Fu, are calling the shots, while other lawmakers are acting as “rubber stamps,” passively obeying the caucus’ decisions, even if they say they are voting based on their conscience or rationality. For example, KMT Legislator Ko Chih-en (柯志恩) expressed her concerns in interviews that cutting the premier’s salary might be against the law, but she still complied with her party’s proposal when it came to a vote.
The political farce carried out by KMT-led lawmakers in the past week vindicates the author of a widely discussed article, “Taking Taiwan’s Democracy Hostage,” in The Economist last week. He said that “a bunch of deeply unimpressive politicians are paralyzing Taiwan’s democracy for shameful, self-interested reasons” and the “KMT-led opposition antics are holding Taiwan politics hostage,” while the only beneficiary is China.
China’s new exit and entry regulations might signal an increase in the risk that Taiwanese travelers will face, an analyst said on Tuesday last week. The new rules, which take effect on Sept. 15, expand the power of authorities to restrict travel on national, industrial and technological security grounds, question travelers about their reasons for leaving and inspect electronic data. Taiwanese who do not support the ruling party should not dismiss the warnings as fearmongering or propaganda. Beijing applies its “anti-secession” laws indiscriminately, an official said recently while presenting a report on proposed amendments to combat China’s efforts at transnational repression. Chinese

Outside of Alphabet Inc’s Google, nearly all of the leading video-generation models are Chinese, making up nine of the top 10 text-to-video systems on benchmarking platform Artificial Analysis’ leaderboard. Trump’s drone tariff deepens decoupling
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:04 UTC
01:41:04 KST

US President Donald Trump’s administration is imposing tariffs of as much as 100 percent on imported drones and their components, escalating efforts to reduce US reliance on foreign suppliers and potentially accelerating a decoupling of drone supply chains with China.
The top rate would apply to heavier drones — weighing more than 25kg — or those that possess certain capabilities, the White House said on Thursday.
Smaller drones would be taxed at 25 percent, while lower rates apply to some trading partners such as the EU and Japan.
Photo: AFP
The statement did not mention China, but the tariffs risk reinforcing a two-way separation with the world’s dominant drone manufacturer already under way. They also add to a drumbeat of tit-for-tat measures just weeks before Chinese leader Xi Jinping (習近平) is expected to meet with Trump in the US.
“In the long term, we’re probably slipping towards an outcome of a hard decoupling for at least certain types of drones,” Gavekal Dragonomics (龍洲經訊) deputy China research director Christopher Beddor said. “I think this is part of a broader pattern in which both the US and China uphold their basic trade agreement, but continue to take relatively low-grade actions against each other.”
US restrictions on new foreign-made models last year have curbed Chinese access to the US market, while Beijing has tightened scrutiny of drone-related exports to the US.
Chinese drone exports to the US fell to about US$50 million in the first half of this year, about half the level recorded a year earlier, Chinese customs data showed.
Last week’s announcement followed other actions aimed at China’s dominance in advanced technology. The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) moved in December last year to block imports of some foreign-made drones including new models from Shenzhen-based DJI Technologies Co (大疆創新), which accounted for about 70 percent of the US commercial drone market last year.
Last month, the FCC banned some foreign-made robots and power inverters.
the curbs provoked retaliation from the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, which placed exports of drones, their key components and related technologies that can be used for military purposes on “strict case-by-case review,” among a barrage of countermeasures.
“This is about reducing dependence on China for advanced drones and importantly components, as previous FCC barriers did not cover imports of grandfathered models and many drone components,” Natixis SA chief economist for Asia Pacific Alicia Garcia-Herrero said.
China exported nearly US$300 million of drone and aircraft parts to the US in the first six months of this year, compared with US$580 million for all of last year, according to the Chinese General Administration of Customs, which does not provide a separate breakdown for drone components.
Smaller drones lacking capabilities deemed especially sensitive for national security would face a 25 percent duty, as would other components. Tariffs on drones from several economies that struck trade deals with Trump would be 15 percent, so long as all hardware and technology originates from those places and the US.
The locations include Taiwan, the EU, Japan and Switzerland. The UK would be subject to a 10 percent tariff on its drones and components.
Most of the levies would take effect in 21 days after Trump signed the proclamation. Tariffs on components that are not considered particularly sensitive would begin after 180 days.

KMT no stranger to corruption
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:41:01 UTC
01:41:01 KST

Each time a major scandal arises, the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) can be counted on to take the first opportunity to twist the narrative and label anyone involved “Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) cronies.”
The controversy around the Central Union Oil Corp’s (CUOC, 中聯油脂) tainted cooking oil scandal is the latest example. According to KMT lawmakers, implicated Fwusow Industry Co (福壽實業) chairman Hung Yau-kuen (洪堯昆) is apparently a “DPP crony” because he had been photographed alongside President William Lai (賴清德). However, all of Hung’s political donations have gone to KMT politicians. He is a former chairman of the board of directors of the Council for Industrial and Commercial Development (工商建研會), a private organization for businesspeople established by the KMT in 1990. Hung, it could be fair to say, seems firmly rooted in the pan-blue camp.
The number of corruption cases related to the green energy sector are too many to count.
KMT Legislator Sra Kacaw (鄭天財) and his legislative office executive director Chang Teng-lung (張騰龍) were indicted last year for accepting bribes including from green energy firms; Yunlin County’s former council speaker Shen Tsung-lung (沈宗隆) of the KMT resigned in 2023 after being implicated in a bribery scandal related to wind farm projects; former KMT central committee member and Tainan local temple chairman, Wang Wen-tsung (王文宗), was indicted in 2023 for harboring a suspect in “88 rounds” shooting, which was tied to a dispute between rival solar power contractors; and last year, former KMT legislator Sufin Siluko (廖國棟) and office director Hung Tien-sheng (洪天盛) were indicted for corruption charges linked to a failed solar project.
On green-energy corruption, it is clear who the instigators often are.
Former Changhua Bar Association chairwoman Chen Yu-hsuan (陳昱瑄) has been indicted for joining forces with others to defraud the Buddhist Compassion Relief Tzu Chi Foundation out of NT$1.06 billion (US$33.1 million) by falsely claiming they could procure Pfizer BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines.
The investigation exposed the lavish lifestyle Chen was enjoying, that she had served as an adviser to the KMT-led Taichung City Government and Changhua County Government, and how she had used her Tzu Chi volunteer status to fuel her bid for chair of the bar association.

Historic Zionist perceptions of Lebanon
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:40:43 UTC
01:40:43 KST

Historic Zionist perceptions of Lebanon
TEHRAN – In southern Lebanon, the occupying Israeli regime is erasing the region’s entire civilizational landscape by demolishing and bulldozing homes, buildings, graves and trees.
Israeli statements are increasingly speaking of no intention to withdraw, plans to establish a broad occupied zone south of the Litani river, evacuate entire areas of their inhabitants, and prevent people from returning to border villages for indefinite periods.
These policies in southern Lebanon are an extension of longstanding Zionist perceptions, based on exploiting internal divisions and seeking control over the south and the Litani.
What the regime is doing raises a historical question that goes beyond the latest aggression: To what extent do current Zionist policies represent a continuation of longstanding perceptions of Lebanon that took shape within the Zionist movement before the establishment of the Israeli regime.
From the earliest days of the Zionist project, Lebanon was not viewed just as a neighboring state to Palestine, but as a special case within the Arab Levant: a space that could be penetrated politically, a potential arena for building alliances with local forces, and a region associated in Zionism’s strategic imagination with water, borders, and minorities.
Laura Zittrain Eisenberg’s study, My Enemy’s Enemy: Lebanon in the Early Zionist Imagination, 1900–1948, shows that an important strand of early Zionist thinking regarded Lebanon as an exception within the Arab environment.
The Zionist movement believed that Lebanon’s sectarian pluralism, the distinctive position of its Maronite community, and its divisions over Arab nationalism and Syrian unity created opportunities for understandings that seemed less attainable elsewhere in the Arab world.
A broad network of contacts was established with Lebanese political and religious figures beginning in the 1920s. These contacts included political, media, and economic figures from across Lebanon’s various sects.
However, the documents specifically mention close relations and cooperation with the Jewish Agency on the part of Maronite Patriarch Antoun Arida, President Emile Edde, Bishop Ignatius Mubarak, and others.
The alliance of minorities and the bet on the Maronites
These contacts were linked to a broader idea that later became known as the “Alliance of Minorities.” The idea was not exclusively Lebanese; rather, it became one of the foundations of subsequent Israeli strategic thinking in the region, which former Zionist intelligence official Yossi Alpher called the “Periphery Doctrine.”
Within this doctrine, Israeli strategic circles believed that the region’s religious or ethnic minorities might share an interest in cooperating with the regime to confront Arab nationalist projects or the centralized states surrounding them.
In Lebanon’s case, this strategy focused primarily on certain Maronite circles. Documents presented by Erlich and Eisenberg indicate that some Lebanese currents viewed the establishment of an occupation regime in Palestine as an additional guarantee for Lebanon’s, which at the time had a Christian political majority.
During the 1940s, discussions also emerged regarding “long-term political cooperation” between the anticipated Zionist regime and certain Lebanese elites opposed to Syrian unity and Arab nationalist currents.
Studies indicate that the Litani River occupied a special place in Zionist thinking even before the establishment of the regime. Zionist leaders believed that the northern borders of Palestine did not reflect what they regarded as the “natural borders” of the regime, and that the Litani River held strategic importance in terms of water, security, and geography.
The discussions were not limited to political alliances between certain Maronite elites and the Zionist movement. They also included ideas for reshaping the demographic reality in the south: settling Maronites in Shia border areas, purchasing large tracts of land in Jabal Amel, creating direct geographical contiguity between Christian areas and Jewish Palestine, and reducing the Shia population density in the area between the Palestinian border and Mount Lebanon.
Against this backdrop, David Ben-Gurion’s diaries are particularly notable. In May 1948, he wrote that Lebanon represented the “weak point” in the Arab alliance, and that a Christian state could be established with the Litani as its southern border and form an alliance with the Zionists.
Early Zionist literature and subsequent Israeli documents reveal a significant degree of continuity in the regime’s view of Lebanon: a field open to political penetration; reliance on allied internal forces; the exceptional importance of southern Lebanon and the Litani; and efforts to create a new security and geographic reality in the border region.
However, the regime’s history of occupation in Lebanon repeatedly demonstrated the limits of its ability to turn these perceptions into a stable political reality or to maintain long-term arrangements serving these strategic aims.
Nevertheless, several projects being proposed today, whether Lebanese-Israeli normalization, the establishment of a so-called “security zone” south of the Litani, or the depopulation of large parts of the south, do not appear disconnected from the long history of perceptions and strategies that accompanied the Zionist project from before the establishment of the Israeli regime.
Yet Lebanon’s complex reality, its internal balances, and the decline of political Maronitism from the position it occupied when those projects were first proposed make the reproduction of these perceptions today far more complicated than some Zionist calculations might suggest.
Equally important, today, Hezbollah resistance stands in the way.

Efe Ozkan
16 August 2026•Update: 16 August 2026
Arsenal began the 2026-27 English football season by defeating Manchester City 3-0 to win the FA Community Shield at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday.
 
Mikel Arteta’s side made a perfect start, taking the lead after just 24 seconds. Debutant Myles Lewis-Skelly surged forward before finding Riccardo Calafiori, whose composed finish marked the fastest goal in Community Shield history.
 
Arsenal continued to dominate the first half and doubled their advantage in the 28th minute. Summer signing Christos Tzolis delivered a pinpoint cross from the left, allowing Kai Havertz to head home and give the Premier League champions a deserved 2-0 lead.
 
Manchester City, playing their first competitive match under new manager Enzo Maresca, enjoyed spells of possession but struggled to create clear-cut chances against Arsenal’s organized defense, while goalkeeper David Raya made key saves to preserve the clean sheet.
 
The Gunners put the result beyond doubt three minutes into the second half. Another flowing team move ended with Tzolis sliding the ball into the path of Martin Odegaard, who calmly finished past the City goalkeeper to make it 3-0.
 
The victory handed Arsenal the first trophy of the new campaign and extended Arteta’s impressive record in the traditional season curtain-raiser, while Maresca’s tenure at Manchester City began with defeat ahead of the Premier League season.
 
The Football Association Community Shield, formerly known as the Charity Shield, is an annual match between the previous season’s Premier League champions and FA Cup winners. Similar to a super cup in other leagues, it traditionally serves as the curtain-raiser for the new English football season.
 
Proceeds from the match are directed toward community initiatives and charitable causes across the country. Revenue is distributed among the 124 clubs that took part in the FA Cup from the first round proper onward, with each club nominating charities or community projects to receive the funds.

Cristiano Ronaldo says this season is likely to be his last as a player after a glittering career.
The 41-year-old married his partner, Georgina Rodriguez, on Tuesday and is contemplating a future orientated around his family.
A five-time Ballon d'Or and five-time Champions League winner, Ronaldo has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia and is the all-time top goalscorer in men's international football.
The Portugal captain has spent almost four years at Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr, where he has one year remaining on his contract.
"This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy," Ronaldo told Vogue in an interview about his wedding.
"I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard. Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.
"Have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned.
"Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."
Ronaldo is 24 goals away from scoring 1,000 senior career goals.
His long-time rival Lionel Messi, who has won the Ballon d'Or accolade a record eight times, recently also said he was unsure how much longer he would continue playing football.
The players' respective World Cup campaigns could hardly have looked more different as Messi scored eight goals and led Argentina all the way to the final, while Ronaldo's Portugal bowed out in the round of 16.
Asked in July whether his sixth World Cup would be his last, Ronaldo said he would decide "with a calm head" in a conversation with his family.
Al-Nassr opened their Saudi Pro League title defence against Al Fateh on Saturday and Ronaldo did not play, but he watched the champions win from the stands with his family.

US attorney general Todd Blanche on Sunday declined to assure that the federal justice department he helms would always act independently of the White House and Donald Trump.
“No, I’m not going to pledge that,” he said when asked about the topic by NBC’s Meet the Press host, Kristen Welker. “And no attorney general should ever pledge that.”
Blanche also claimed Trump would never ask him to do something that crosses an ethical or legal line – after the president dismissed his predecessor, Pam Bondi, having become frustrated over insufficient action from the justice department against Trump’s political foes.
“The president will never ask me to do something unethical or legal or illegal,” Blanche told Welker. “He never has. He never will. And no, I have – I swore to the constitution of the United States, like every cabinet secretary has done, and like every attorney general before me has done.
“And so, this narrative that’s mostly pushed by the left and pushed by the media that the president’s going to pull me aside and ask me to do something illegal is completely a false narrative, not true, will not happen and hasn’t happened.”
In response to his demurring on the questions of always acting independently of the White House, Barb McQuade, a University of Michigan law professor, wrote on social media that Blanche’s stated position was “an appalling departure” from the justice department’s mission after the Watergate scandal that prompted Richard Nixon to resign from the presidency in 1974.
The justice department, “as we once knew it, is no more”, McQuade wrote. “Blanche has turned it into Trump’s private law firm. What a complete disgrace.”
Blanche’s comments to Welker on Sunday came days after he was only narrowly confirmed by the US Senate in a 50-49 vote to succeed Bondi, with all Democrats voting against him. He previously served as Trump’s criminal defense lawyer when a New York state jury convicted Trump between his two presidencies of 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in connection with payments to adult film star Stormy Daniels.
In April, Blanche said he would tell Trump, “I love you, sir,” if the president decided to fire him and nominate someone else to replace Bondi.
Blanche, meanwhile, in December defended moving Ghislaine Maxwell, the convicted child sexual trafficker and Jeffrey Epstein associate, to a minimum-security prison. And Blanche has also continued facing scrutiny over his handling of the so-called Epstein files and his treatment of those victimized by the sex-trafficking network built by Epstein.
While speaking with Welker on Sunday, Blanche also defended Trump’s pardoning of 1,500 supporters who were convicted of attacking the US Capitol toward the end of his first presidency in early 2021.
“I’m not opining or in any way saying what President Trump did was wrong,” Blanche said when asked about the pardons, which included more than 170 people who pleaded guilty to assaulting police officers. “That is the president’s right.”
Blanche declined to say whether any of the pardoned attackers might still receive settlements from the federal government – though they attorney general also claimed a $1.8bn “anti-weaponization” fund for allies whom Trump considered to be unfairly prosecuted was dead.
“Well, anybody can file a claim against the federal government, not just anybody associated with [the Capitol attack],” Blanche said. “I’m not going to sit here and say on a news program whether a litigation that may or may not happen will result in money. I can’t do that.”
He also affirmed the justice department would not drop “election integrity” efforts despite more than 20 consecutive court defeats connected to efforts to try to force states to turn over voter rolls ahead of the midterm elections in November, when the president’s Republican party is projected to lose seats in Congress and favored to lose the majority in the US House.

Water companies in England and Wales explore ‘surge pricing’ during drought
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
16:28:00 UTC
01:28:00 KST

Water companies could be allowed to raise bills for customers during periods of drought under proposals being considered by the sector’s regulator for England and Wales.
Suppliers would be permitted to factor “water scarcity” into bills as part of efforts to reduce consumption under Ofwat’s plans, which are being likened to surge pricing – the practice where private hire firms raise taxi fares at times of higher demand.
The proposals come just a few days after the prime minster, Andy Burnham, said he was angry with water companies and accused them of treating their customers like a “blank cheque” after more than a dozen firms were given the green light to raise water bills even higher.
It emerged last Thursday that five companies – Southern Water, Thames Water, Severn Trent, Wessex Water and South East Water – would be allowed to raise bills more than originally planned before the end of the decade to allow for billions of pounds of extra spending on repairs and infrastructure.
The surge pricing proposals, first reported by the Sunday Telegraph, come after the 30 July conclusion of Ofwat’s consultation on changing the rules relating to wholesale charging, with the regulator due to share its final decision shortly.
Public anger over the behaviour of water companies has soared in recent years as bills have continued to climb even while sewage has flowed into the nation’s waterways and firms have increased bosses’ pay and handed out millions of pounds in dividends to shareholders.
During an exceptionally hot and dry summer, leading to almost three-quarters of England and all of Wales being declared officially in drought, suppliers have also come under fire for failing to save water lost through leaky pipes, which campaigners say far outstrips the amount that could be saved through a nationwide hosepipe ban.
An Ofwat spokesperson said: “The efficient use of water is in the best interests of everyone, including businesses. The options we are progressing would support greater consideration of water scarcity and efficiency by water companies when setting their charges, and encourage more tariff innovation.”
Several water companies have been carrying out charging trials over the past few years aimed at making bills more affordable and, potentially, reducing demand.
South West Water, which supplies water to about 1.8 million customers across south-west England, including Cornwall and Devon, is trialling a “rising block tariff”, where about 500 household customers are charged a cheaper rate for using a lower amount (or “block”) of water and progressively higher prices for higher consumption.
The company said 90% of its customers would see lower bills on this trial, according to its assessments.
Anglian Water, which supplies 7 million customers across the east of England, the UK’s driest region, and South West Water are also trialling charging customers more for water used in the summer than in the winter months.
The Guardian understands there are no government plans for nationwide surge pricing for water bills.
A government spokesperson said: “Water companies are trialling new charging structures which must, as promised, make bills fairer and more affordable while encouraging greater water efficiency.”
They added: “We have already ringfenced money earmarked for new infrastructure so it can only be spent on fixing the problems, and will go further by fundamentally reforming the water sector so that it works for the public, keeping bills as low as they can be.”
Andy White, a senior lead for social policy at the Consumer Council for Water (CCW), a government-sponsored body that represents customers’ interests, said water companies were right to explore new tariff structures that could help manage demand and give customers more control over their bills.
He said: “Any new approach must be fair and protect customers who are already struggling with rising water costs. None of the schemes currently being trialled are designed to generate additional revenue for water companies, and many are structured so that most customers will pay less overall.”
White added that companies should give consumers smart meter data to give them a clearer picture of how they use water.
A spokesperson for Water UK, the industry’s trade association, said companies were working to cut down on leaks, adding: “We also need to consider whether we could help people save water by rewarding people through their water bill. This might include eliminating standing charges or expanding discounts for customers who save water.”

Search teams comb rubble in Colombia nearly a week after quake as aid effort expands

The 7.4-magnitude quake struck Monday morning in San Jose del Palmar, causing severe damage from the Pacific port of Buenaventura to Colombia's coffee-growing region and major western cities including Cali and Pereira.
Official estimates issued on Sunday put the death toll at around 290, with more than 140 people still missing and 4,200 injured. More than two-thirds of the deaths were concentrated in Cali and Pereira, where apartment blocks, homes, churches, schools and hospitals were damaged or destroyed.
In Cali, Colombia's third-largest city, emergency workers continued searching unstable piles of concrete and twisted metal on Sunday as rescue efforts increasingly gave way to the recovery of bodies.
"Unfortunately, there are no signs of life," Cali fire department Captain Alberto Hernandez said. "Miracles can happen, but honestly - as a believer and based on what we have seen - there is no indication that anyone is still alive."
Aftershocks have added to the danger for crews working in damaged neighborhoods and for residents still unable to return home.
"Work has to be done very carefully and methodically... so we do not put rescuers or community members helping at the site at further risk," Hernandez added.
As hopes of finding more survivors dimmed, the relief operation was expanding.
In Bogota, a stadium has been turned into the country's biggest donation collection center, while in Pereira authorities were treating injured pets and distributing donated animal food.
"Horrible, it's overwhelming," said Claudia Galeano, 53, who lost her home in Pereira. Her father, Arnulfo Galeano, was pulled alive from the rubble but later died in hospital.
"The earthquake took my father from me, but there are people worse off than me, left on the street, without family, without anything."
The quake is the first major crisis facing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who took office just days before the disaster and now faces the task of overseeing relief and reconstruction.
De La Espriella said on Sunday that Colombian billionaire banker Jaime Gilinski, who also controls food company Nutresa, would donate 150 billion pesos ($47.75 million) to rebuild hospitals and schools in Gilinski's hometown Cali. The Santo Domingo family, which controls a vast media empire in the nation, had already pledged $32 million on Friday. REUTERS
